listening.title: Joining a community sports centre
listening.titleVi: Đăng ký thẻ hội viên trung tâm thể thao
listening.context: A woman phones a community sports centre to register for a membership.

script.say: Part 1. You will hear a woman phoning a community sports centre to register for membership. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 8.

script.t: Good afternoon, Ashcombe Community Sports Centre, Daniel speaking. How can I help?
Oh, hello. I'd like to sign up for a membership, if that's possible over the phone.
Yes, of course. I can take your details now, and then you just pop in to collect your card. Can I start with your name?
Sure. It's Joanna Caulfield.
Could you spell the surname for me, please?
Yes, it's C, A, U, L, F, I, E, L, D.
Thanks. And what is your address, Ms Caulfield?
It's 42 Linnet Road. That's Linnet like the bird – L, I, N, N, E, T.
Lovely. And that's here in Ashcombe?
Yes, just behind the library, near the primary school.
Great. And a contact phone number?
My home phone doesn't really get used any more, so my mobile is best.
Let me read that back to you. 0, 7, 7, 3, 4 – 5, 9, 2, 6, 1, 8?
That's right.
OK, so what kind of membership were you thinking of?
Well, I was going to get an individual one, just for me. But my son is eleven, and he really wants to come too.
In that case, a family membership might be better value. It covers two adults and up to three children.
Oh, right. Yes, let's go for the family one, then. My husband might use it as well.
How much does that cost? Your website said forty-five pounds a month.
That's the standard family rate, which lets you come in at any time of day.
But if you only use the centre during off-peak hours, it's thirty-eight pounds a month.
And off-peak is when, exactly?
Before five o'clock on weekdays, and all day at weekends.
That suits us fine. I work from home, so I'll go for the off-peak one.
Good choice. And when would you like the membership to start?
Could it start on the 13th of March?
Oh no, sorry – that's the week we're away visiting my parents. Let's say the 15th, not the 13th.
No problem at all. The 15th of March it is.
Now, is there any particular activity you're most interested in? It helps us plan our classes.
I used to swim a lot, but these days it's mainly badminton. I play with a friend from work.
Great, we have courts free most mornings. And finally, how did you hear about us? Was it online?
No, actually. Someone put a leaflet through my door last month, and it had all the prices on it.

script.say: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 9 and 10.

script.t: Right, that's the form done. When you come in for the first time, you'll need to bring a couple of things.
Do you need proof of address? I've got a bank statement somewhere.
We don't need that, because you're paying by direct debit and the bank checks it.
But we do need a passport-sized photo for your membership card.
OK, a photo. I can do that. Anything else?
No, that's all. Now, you mentioned your son. Is he interested in anything in particular?
He was hoping to try the junior swimming course.
I'm afraid that's full until the summer. But we've just opened a climbing wall.
There's a free taster session for under-fourteens on Saturday morning. I'd really recommend that.
Oh, he'd love that. What about football? He's mentioned your summer camp.
Bookings for that don't open until May, so I'd start with the climbing.
Perfect. Thanks so much for your help, Daniel.
My pleasure. See you on the 15th.

groups.title: Ashcombe Community Sports Centre – Membership form
groups.instr: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.cue: C, A, U, L, F, I, E, L, D
items.explain: Joanna đánh vần họ của mình: “C, A, U, L, F, I, E, L, D”. Cần nghe kỹ từng chữ cái, dễ viết nhầm thành “Colfield” hoặc “Caufield”.

items.cue: L, I, N, N, E, T
items.explain: Địa chỉ là “42 Linnet Road”, được đánh vần “L, I, N, N, E, T” (giống tên loài chim). Lưu ý có hai chữ N; số 42 đã cho sẵn.
Số di động được đọc rồi nhắc lại để xác nhận: “0, 7, 7, 3, 4 – 5, 9, 2, 6, 1, 8”. Bẫy: cô nhắc đến “home phone” nhưng nói số đó gần như không dùng.

items.cue: let's go for the family one
items.explain: Ban đầu Joanna định chọn “an individual one”, nhưng sau khi nghe tư vấn cô đổi ý: “let's go for the family one”. Đáp án là family, không phải individual.

items.cue: it's thirty-eight pounds a month
items.explain: Bẫy: “forty-five pounds a month” là giá tiêu chuẩn. Giá giờ thấp điểm (off-peak) là “thirty-eight pounds a month”, và cô chọn gói này.

items.cue: Let's say the 15th
items.explain: Joanna nói ngày 13 rồi tự sửa: “Let's say the 15th, not the 13th”, nhân viên xác nhận “The 15th of March”. Ngày 13 là bẫy.

items.cue: it's mainly badminton
items.explain: Bẫy: cô “used to swim a lot” (trước đây), còn hiện nay “it's mainly badminton”. “Main activity” được diễn đạt lại bằng “mainly”.

items.text: Heard about the centre from a ___
items.cue: put a leaflet through my door
items.explain: Nhân viên hỏi có phải biết qua mạng (“online”) không; cô phủ nhận và nói “Someone put a leaflet through my door”. Đáp án là leaflet.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: What must Joanna bring on her first visit?
items.cue: a passport-sized photo
items.explain: Đáp án B: “we do need a passport-sized photo” (= a photograph). A sai vì “bank statement” là giấy chứng minh địa chỉ, nhân viên nói “We don't need that”; C (thẻ ngân hàng) không được nhắc đến.

items.q: What does Daniel recommend for Joanna's son?
items.cue: free taster session for under-fourteens
items.explain: Đáp án B: Daniel nói về “a free taster session for under-fourteens” ở tường leo núi và “I'd really recommend that”. A sai vì khóa bơi “full until the summer”; C sai vì trại hè bóng đá “don't open until May”.

vocab.vi: giấy tờ chứng minh địa chỉ
ghi nợ tự động (trích tiền tài khoản)

listening.title: A restored market hall
listening.titleVi: Tham quan khu chợ cổ được trùng tu
listening.context: A guide welcomes a group of visitors to a restored nineteenth-century market hall.

script.say: Part 2. You will hear a guide talking to a group of visitors at a restored market hall. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.

script.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Wendlebury Market Hall. My name's Kirsty, and I'll be showing you around today.
Before we start walking, I'll give you a bit of background, and then some practical information about what you can see and do here.
The whole tour takes about forty minutes, and there'll be plenty of time for questions at the end, so don't be shy.
The hall was built in 1868, and it's one of the few covered markets of its kind still standing in the region.
A lot of visitors assume it was a fish market, because of the cold stone floors and the drains you can still see.
But in fact, it was built for the wool trade. Farmers brought fleeces down from the hills every Tuesday.
And merchants travelled from all over the country to buy them. For about fifty years, this was the busiest building in town.
Fish was sold here later, from around the 1920s, but only ever in one corner of the hall.
By the 1980s, the building was in a terrible state, and for nearly twenty years it was closed to the public.
Then a local trust raised the money to restore it. The original plan was to finish the work in three years.
Well, as often happens with old buildings, it ended up taking five, and we finally reopened two years ago.
People often ask me what the hardest part of the job was. You'd probably guess the glass roof, since it's so huge.
But actually, the roof panels were fairly simple to replace. The real challenge was the iron columns holding everything up.
Each one had to be taken down, repaired by hand and put back exactly where it came from, and some of them were badly cracked.
Now, one small request. The floor tiles near the main entrance are original, and they're quite fragile.
You're very welcome to walk on them, and to take photos, but please don't wheel heavy bags or pushchairs across them.
There's a ramp to the right of the entrance that you can use instead.
The tiles were made in a local factory that closed long ago, so if one breaks, we simply cannot replace it.

script.say: Now look at questions 15 to 20.

script.t: OK, so let me tell you about the different parts of the hall and what's on offer.
First, the clock tower. You can climb right to the top, and the view across the river is wonderful on a clear day.
But the staircase is narrow, so we only take groups of eight, and you'll need to reserve a place at the information desk beforehand.
Next, the café, which is in the old weighing room. It's open every day from nine, and it normally stays open until six.
On Fridays, though, it closes at three, because the room is used for evening events.
Then there are the craft workshops, where you can watch local weavers and potters at work, and even try a little yourself.
Some people think you have to book these, but you don't. Just bear in mind that they only run on Saturdays and Sundays.
The history gallery is something we're very proud of. It used to be on the ground floor, by the main doors.
But it's now upstairs, in the east gallery, where there's more space and better light for the displays.
If you've got coats or bags you'd like to leave, there are lockers beside the toilets.
Normally they cost a dollar coin, but if you show your entry ticket at the desk, you can use one without paying.
And finally, for anyone with little ones, there's the play corner near the old fish stalls.
It's got soft flooring and small wooden stalls the kids can play shop with, so it's ideal for under-fives.
The lift to the upper floor is being repaired at the moment, by the way, but that should be finished next week.
Right, if you'd like to follow me, we'll start with those columns I mentioned earlier.
Oh, and one last thing – the gift shop by the exit sells wool from local farms, which seems fitting, given the history of the place.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: The market hall was originally built for
items.cue: it was built for the wool trade
items.explain: Đáp án B: “it was built for the wool trade” (= trading wool). A là bẫy: nhiều người tưởng là chợ cá, nhưng cá chỉ được bán “later” ở một góc. C không được nhắc đến (nông dân mang lông cừu, không phải gia súc).

items.q: How long did the restoration take?
items.cue: it ended up taking five
items.explain: Đáp án B: kế hoạch ban đầu là “three years” nhưng “it ended up taking five”. C sai vì “nearly twenty years” là thời gian tòa nhà bị đóng cửa, không phải thời gian trùng tu.

items.q: According to the guide, the most difficult part of the restoration was
items.cue: The real challenge was the iron columns
items.explain: Đáp án B: “The real challenge was the iron columns” (= most difficult part). A là bẫy: người ta hay đoán mái kính, nhưng tấm mái “fairly simple to replace”; C (lau sàn đá) không được nhắc đến.

items.q: Visitors are asked to
options: keep wheeled items off the original tiles.
leave large bags at the entrance.
items.cue: please don't wheel heavy bags or pushchairs across them
items.explain: Đáp án B: “please don't wheel heavy bags or pushchairs across them” = giữ đồ có bánh xe tránh xa nền gạch cổ. A sai vì khách “welcome… to take photos”; C sai vì không ai yêu cầu để túi ở cửa.

groups.instr: What does the guide say about each part of the market hall? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to questions 15–20.
options: D suitable for very young children
E must be booked in advance
F closes early on one day

items.cue: reserve a place at the information desk beforehand
items.explain: Đáp án E: với tháp đồng hồ, khách “need to reserve a place at the information desk beforehand” (= must be booked in advance). Chi tiết nhóm tối đa tám người chỉ là thông tin phụ.

items.cue: On Fridays, though, it closes at three
items.explain: Đáp án F: quán café thường mở đến sáu giờ, nhưng “On Fridays, though, it closes at three” (= closes early on one day). Café mở cửa mọi ngày nên không phải A.

items.cue: they only run on Saturdays and Sundays
items.explain: Đáp án A: các xưởng thủ công “only run on Saturdays and Sundays” (= only open at weekends). Bẫy E: hướng dẫn viên nói rõ không cần đặt trước: “you don't”.

items.cue: it's now upstairs, in the east gallery
items.explain: Đáp án C: phòng trưng bày lịch sử “used to be on the ground floor” nhưng “it's now upstairs, in the east gallery” (= has changed location).

items.cue: you can use one without paying
items.explain: Đáp án B: tủ khóa thường tốn “a dollar coin”, nhưng “if you show your entry ticket… you can use one without paying” (= free for ticket holders).

items.cue: ideal for under-fives
items.explain: Đáp án D: khu vui chơi “ideal for under-fives” (= suitable for very young children). Bẫy G: thứ “being repaired” là thang máy (“The lift”), không phải khu vui chơi.

vocab.vi: quỹ bảo tồn (tổ chức phi lợi nhuận)

listening.title: Food waste in university canteens
listening.titleVi: Dự án nghiên cứu lãng phí thức ăn ở căng tin
listening.context: Two students, Maya and Oliver, discuss the draft of their research report with their tutor, Dr Haines.

script.say: Part 3. You will hear two students, Maya and Oliver, talking to their tutor about their research project on food waste in university canteens. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.

script.t: Come in, both of you. So, you've sent me the draft of your food waste report. How are you feeling about it?
Pretty good, I think. It's been a lot more work than we expected, though.
Yeah, the data collection alone took ages. We were weighing bins every day for three weeks.
Let's go back to the beginning for a moment. Remind me why you chose university canteens as your focus.
Well, I worked in the canteen here in my first year, so I'd seen how much food got thrown away.
That was part of it. But the main thing was that when we searched the literature, there was almost nothing on universities.
Loads on schools and hospitals, but hardly any studies of student canteens. So it seemed like a real gap.
That is a good justification. Make sure you state it clearly in the introduction.
We will. We also thought it would be easier to get access, since we could just ask the catering manager here.
Yes, and that's a perfectly sensible practical reason, but it's not the one to lead with.
And what did the waste audit itself show? Was there anything you didn't expect?
Definitely. I'd assumed the biggest problem would be meat, because it's the most expensive thing they serve.
But it was actually the vegetable side dishes. Students would take them with the set meal and then leave most of them on the plate.
Interesting. And by weight, that was the largest category?
Yes, by quite a long way. Meat was only third, after bread.
Now, your student survey. I think it's a useful part of the project, but there's one problem with it.
Is it the number of people? We only got about two hundred responses.
No, two hundred is perfectly adequate for a project of this size. And the questions were nicely neutral.
The issue is that you only handed out the questionnaires at lunchtime. Students who eat in the evening might behave quite differently.
Oh, that's true. The evening crowd is mostly postgraduates, and they tend to eat bigger meals.
Exactly. You don't need to redo the survey, but you should mention it as a limitation in your discussion.
You also looked at changes the canteens tried out during the term. Which ones did they actually test?
So, the first was taking away the trays. The idea is that if you can't carry so much, you don't take so much.
And the second was an app where students could order their meal in advance, so the kitchen knew how much to cook.
Didn't they also talk about using smaller plates?
They discussed it, but the new plates didn't arrive in time, so that never happened.
And there were going to be posters about waste, but the students' union said no to that.
And charging for second helpings?
That was never really an option. Second helpings already cost extra here.

script.say: Now look at questions 26 to 30.

script.t: OK, let's go through the sections of the report one by one. I've made some notes.
The introduction is fine in terms of content, but it's far too long. You could easily cut it by half.
And the literature review? I was a bit worried about that one.
No need. It's very well organised – you've grouped the studies by theme, which makes it easy to follow.
What about the methodology?
That's where I'd like more. At the moment, a reader couldn't repeat your study.
Explain exactly how you weighed the waste, and at what times.
We put all the daily figures in the main text. Is that too much?
It is. The tables are useful, but they interrupt the reading. Put them at the end, in an appendix, and just refer to them.
And the results section? We worked really hard on the writing there.
And it shows – the style is good, so leave that as it is.
But the comparison between the three canteens would be much clearer as a graph or a chart.
OK, that's really helpful. We'll get started on those changes this week.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: Why did the students choose university canteens as their topic?
options: Little research had been done on it.
Maya had worked in a canteen.
items.cue: hardly any studies of student canteens
items.explain: Đáp án C: Oliver nói lý do chính là “there was almost nothing on universities… hardly any studies of student canteens” (= little research). A là bẫy: Maya từng làm ở căng tin, nhưng đó chỉ là “part of it”; B không được nhắc đến.

items.q: What surprised the students about the waste audit?
options: Bread was hardly wasted at all.
Meat was the most wasted food.
Vegetables were wasted more than other food.
items.cue: it was actually the vegetable side dishes
items.explain: Đáp án B: “it was actually the vegetable side dishes”, lượng lãng phí lớn nhất “by quite a long way”. A là điều Oliver “assumed” nhưng sai, thịt “only third”; C sai vì bánh mì đứng thứ hai.

items.q: What does the tutor think is the weakness of the survey?
options: It was carried out at only one time of day.
items.cue: you only handed out the questionnaires at lunchtime
items.explain: Đáp án C: vấn đề là “you only handed out the questionnaires at lunchtime” (= only one time of day). A sai vì “two hundred is perfectly adequate”; B sai vì câu hỏi “nicely neutral”.

groups.instr: Choose TWO letters, A–E.
groups.q: Which TWO changes did the canteens actually trial?
groups.cue: the first was taking away the trays
groups.explain: Đáp án B và E: “taking away the trays” (= removing trays) và “an app… order their meal in advance”. A sai vì đĩa mới “didn't arrive in time”; D bị hội sinh viên “said no”; C sai vì phần thêm “already cost extra”.

groups.instr: What is the tutor's opinion of each section of the report? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 26–30.
options: C should be moved to an appendix
F should be written more formally

items.cue: it's far too long
items.explain: Đáp án B: phần mở đầu “far too long. You could easily cut it by half” (= should be shortened). Nội dung thì “fine”, nên không cần thêm chi tiết.

items.cue: It's very well organised
items.explain: Đáp án D: tổng quan tài liệu “very well organised” vì đã nhóm các nghiên cứu theo chủ đề. Oliver lo lắng nhưng giảng viên nói “No need”.

items.cue: That's where I'd like more.
items.explain: Đáp án A: với phần phương pháp, “That's where I'd like more”, người đọc chưa thể lặp lại nghiên cứu, cần “Explain exactly how you weighed the waste” (= needs more detail).

items.cue: Put them at the end, in an appendix
items.explain: Đáp án C: các bảng số liệu hằng ngày làm gián đoạn việc đọc, nên “Put them at the end, in an appendix”.

items.cue: would be much clearer as a graph or a chart
items.explain: Đáp án E: phần kết quả nên trình bày phép so sánh ba căng tin “as a graph or a chart” (= needs a visual). Bẫy F: văn phong “good, so leave that as it is”, không cần viết trang trọng hơn.

vocab.vi: các tài liệu/nghiên cứu đã có

listening.title: Green roofs in cities
listening.titleVi: Mái nhà xanh trong đô thị
listening.context: A lecture on how cities use green roofs to manage heat and rainwater.

script.say: Part 4. You will hear a lecture about how cities use green roofs. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

script.t: Good morning. Today we're looking at green roofs, and why more and more cities are encouraging them.
We'll cover what they are, how they help with heat and with rainwater, and finally some of the problems they bring.
So, first, what exactly is a green roof? Basically, it's a roof that's partly or completely covered with plants.
But you can't just put soil on top of a building. The most important layer is a waterproof membrane, which protects the structure underneath.
Above that, there's usually a drainage layer, then a growing medium – a kind of lightweight soil – and finally the plants themselves.
Broadly speaking, there are two main types. Extensive green roofs have a very thin layer of soil, often less than fifteen centimetres.
Because of that, they're usually planted with sedum, a small plant that stores water in its leaves and survives long dry periods.
Grasses are sometimes used as well, but they tend to struggle in a hot summer.
Extensive roofs are relatively cheap and light, which is why they are by far the most common type on existing buildings.
Intensive green roofs are quite different. They have deep soil and can support shrubs and even small trees, rather like a park.
They look wonderful, but they need regular maintenance – watering, weeding, pruning – just like any garden at ground level.
Let's turn now to heat. You've probably heard of the urban heat island effect.
That's the fact that cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, especially at night.
Dark roofs absorb a huge amount of sunlight and release it as heat. Green roofs reduce this in two ways.
The plants do provide some shade, of course. But the main cooling effect comes from evaporation.
As water leaves the soil and the leaves, it takes heat with it, in the same way that sweat cools our skin.
The difference can be dramatic. On a hot afternoon, a conventional roof might reach seventy degrees Celsius.
Studies have found that a green roof can bring the surface temperature down by as much as thirty degrees.
That's thirty – not three, as it's sometimes misquoted in the newspapers.
And this affects the people inside, too. Top-floor rooms stay cooler, so there is less need for air conditioning.
For building owners, that means lower electricity bills, which is often the argument that persuades them.
The second big benefit concerns rainwater. In a city, most surfaces are hard – roads, pavements, roofs – so rain cannot soak into the ground.
During heavy storms, the drains simply cannot cope, and the result is flooding in the streets.
A green roof acts a bit like a sponge. It holds a large part of the rain and releases it slowly, which reduces that risk considerably.
There is a further advantage. The water that does run off is cleaner, because the soil and roots work as a natural filter.
They trap dust and some of the pollutants that would otherwise end up in rivers.
Green roofs also support wildlife. Ecologists have recorded bees, butterflies and other insects on roofs many storeys high.
Birds visit them too, but much less often than you might expect.
Some researchers now design roofs specifically for wildlife, using a mix of local wild flowers rather than a single plant.
So, why doesn't every building have one? Well, the biggest problem is weight.
When the soil is soaked with rain, a green roof can be extremely heavy, and many older buildings were never designed to carry that load.
They may need expensive strengthening before a green roof can be installed.
Leaks are another worry for owners, although with a good membrane they are actually quite rare.
Cost is an issue as well, of course, but prices are falling as the technology becomes more common.
In our next session, we'll look at some of the policies cities have introduced to overcome these problems.

groups.title: Green roofs
groups.instr: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.text: Structure: plants grown above a waterproof ___ that protects the building
items.cue: waterproof membrane
items.explain: Giảng viên nói lớp quan trọng nhất là “a waterproof membrane, which protects the structure underneath”. “Structure underneath” được diễn đạt lại thành “protects the building”.

items.text: Extensive roofs: thin soil; usually planted with ___
items.cue: they're usually planted with sedum
items.explain: Mái mở rộng (extensive) có đất mỏng nên “they're usually planted with sedum”. Bẫy: “Grasses” đôi khi cũng được dùng nhưng không phải loại thường gặp.

items.text: Intensive roofs: deep soil, shrubs and small trees; need regular ___
items.cue: they need regular maintenance
items.explain: Mái thâm canh (intensive) “need regular maintenance – watering, weeding, pruning”. Các từ watering, weeding chỉ là ví dụ minh họa, đáp án là danh từ chung maintenance.

items.text: Heat: main cooling effect is caused by ___
items.cue: the main cooling effect comes from evaporation
items.explain: Cây có tạo bóng mát (“shade”) nhưng đó là tác dụng phụ; “the main cooling effect comes from evaporation”. Bẫy: shade.

items.text: Roof surface can be up to ___ degrees cooler
items.cue: as much as thirty degrees
items.explain: Mái xanh giảm nhiệt độ bề mặt “by as much as thirty degrees”, giảng viên nhấn mạnh “thirty – not three”. Bẫy: “seventy degrees” là nhiệt độ của mái thường.

items.cue: lower electricity bills
items.explain: Phòng tầng trên mát hơn nên ít dùng điều hòa, nghĩa là “lower electricity bills” cho chủ tòa nhà. “Lower” được diễn đạt lại thành “reduced”.

items.text: Rainwater: roof holds rain and releases it slowly, so less ___ in streets
items.cue: the result is flooding in the streets
items.explain: Khi mưa lớn, cống quá tải và “the result is flooding in the streets”; mái xanh giữ nước như miếng bọt biển nên giảm rủi ro này.

items.text: Soil and roots act as a ___, so run-off is cleaner
items.cue: work as a natural filter
items.explain: Nước chảy ra sạch hơn vì “the soil and roots work as a natural filter”. Câu hỏi dùng “act as” thay cho “work as”.

items.text: Wildlife: habitat for bees, butterflies and other ___
items.cue: butterflies and other insects
items.explain: Các nhà sinh thái ghi nhận “bees, butterflies and other insects” trên mái nhà. Bẫy: “Birds” cũng được nhắc nhưng “much less often”, và không khớp với cụm “bees, butterflies”.

items.text: Main problem: the ___ of the roof, especially for older buildings
items.cue: the biggest problem is weight
items.explain: “the biggest problem is weight” (= main problem), nhất là với các tòa nhà cũ không được thiết kế để chịu tải đó. Bẫy: leaks (rò rỉ) và cost (chi phí) là các vấn đề phụ.

listening.title: Booking a weekend photography course
listening.titleVi: Đăng ký khóa học nhiếp ảnh cuối tuần
listening.context: A woman phones a photography school to ask about a weekend course for beginners.

script.say: Part 1. You will hear a woman phoning a photography school to ask about a weekend course. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 7.

script.t: Hi there, Lakeview Lens Studio, this is Dan. How can I help?
Oh, hello. I'm interested in one of your weekend photography courses.
Great. We've got a few running this autumn. Do you know which one you're after?
I think it's the one for beginners. Something about landscapes?
Right, that'd be Outdoor Basics. It's aimed at people who've just bought their first proper camera.
That's me. My husband gave me one for my birthday and, honestly, I've no idea what half the buttons do.
Then you're definitely in the right place. Let me take a few details first, OK?
Sure.
Can I get your full name?
It's Rachel Thornbury.
Could you spell the last name for me?
Yes, it's T, H, O, R, N, B, U, R, Y.
Thanks. And what’s the best number to reach you on?
Got it. And can I ask how you heard about us?
Well, I picked up one of your leaflets at the library, but actually it was my neighbour who recommended you.
She did a course with you last spring and loved it.
Oh, that's nice to hear. I'll make a note of that.
OK, so about the course itself. Outdoor Basics runs on a Saturday and Sunday, from nine thirty until four.
And when is the next one?
The next one with spaces is the weekend of the 18th of October.
Oh, I'm away that weekend, unfortunately. Is there another one after that?
Let me look. There's the 25th… no, sorry, the 25th is completely full.
After that, the next one starts on the 1st of November. There are three places left.
The 1st of November is perfect. Can I have one of those?
Sure. Now, one thing people often get wrong: the course doesn't start at our studio.
Because it's an outdoor course, everyone meets in the car park at Hollins Reservoir.
Hollins? How do you spell that?
H, O, L, L, I, N, S. It's about ten minutes' drive from town.
OK. And what does it cost?
The standard charge for the weekend is one hundred and sixty pounds.
Oh. That's a bit more than I was expecting.
Well, if you have a library card, we give a discount, so it comes down to one hundred and forty-five.
Oh, I do have one, yes.
Great. And that price covers lunch on both days, plus a framed print of your best picture at the end.
Oh, that's a lovely idea.

script.say: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 8 to 10.

script.t: Is there anything I need to bring? I was wondering about a tripod.
No need for that, we've got plenty to lend. And camera batteries usually last all day.
But the weather up by the reservoir changes really fast, so definitely bring a waterproof jacket.
Right. And who will be teaching?
Your tutor is Maria Costa. People often ask if she's written books – she hasn't.
But she spent fifteen years taking pictures for a local newspaper before she started teaching.
She's been shortlisted for a couple of national prizes, too, though she hasn't won one yet.
She sounds great. So, can I pay by card now, over the phone?
I'm afraid we can't take card payments over the phone at the moment.
You can do a bank transfer, or bring cash on the first morning.
I'd rather not carry that much cash around. I'll do the transfer this evening.
Perfect. I'll email you our bank details and a map right now.
Thanks so much, Dan. Bye!

groups.title: Lakeview Lens Studio – Course booking
groups.instr: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.cue: T, H, O, R, N, B, U, R, Y
items.explain: Rachel đánh vần họ của mình: “T, H, O, R, N, B, U, R, Y” → Thornbury. Chú ý chép đúng từng chữ cái, đặc biệt cụm “BURY” ở cuối.
Rachel đọc số di động: “0, 7, 9, 1, 2 – 4, 4, 6, 3, 0, 8”. Hai số 4 liền nhau được đọc riêng từng chữ; nghe kỹ để không bỏ sót chữ số nào.

items.text: Heard about the school from her ___
items.cue: my neighbour who recommended you
items.explain: Bẫy: cô ấy có nhắc “one of your leaflets at the library” (tờ rơi ở thư viện), nhưng sau đó nói “but actually it was my neighbour who recommended you” → đáp án là neighbour.

items.cue: the next one starts on the 1st of November
items.explain: Ngày 18/10 cô ấy bận, ngày 25 thì “completely full”. Đáp án là khóa sau đó: “the next one starts on the 1st of November”, và Rachel xác nhận “The 1st of November is perfect”.

items.text: Meeting point: car park at ___ Reservoir
items.cue: H, O, L, L, I, N, S
items.explain: Khóa học không bắt đầu ở studio mà tập trung “in the car park at Hollins Reservoir”; Dan đánh vần “H, O, L, L, I, N, S”.

items.cue: one hundred and forty-five
items.explain: Bẫy số: giá chuẩn là “one hundred and sixty pounds” (£160), nhưng có thẻ thư viện thì được giảm còn “one hundred and forty-five” → 145, và Rachel xác nhận có thẻ.

items.text: Price includes: lunch and a ___ of her best picture
items.cue: a framed print of your best picture
items.explain: Giá đã bao gồm bữa trưa cả hai ngày “plus a framed print of your best picture” → framed print (ảnh in có khung). Từ “includes” trong đề tương ứng với “covers” trong bài.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: What does Dan advise Rachel to bring?
items.cue: definitely bring a waterproof jacket
items.explain: Đáp án C: Dan nói “definitely bring a waterproof jacket” vì thời tiết đổi nhanh. A sai vì tripod thì “No need for that, we've got plenty to lend”; B sai vì pin “usually last all day”.

items.q: What does Dan say about the tutor, Maria Costa?
options: She used to work for a newspaper.
items.cue: taking pictures for a local newspaper
items.explain: Đáp án B: cô ấy “spent fifteen years taking pictures for a local newspaper” – tức từng làm cho báo. A sai: viết sách thì “she hasn't”; C sai: chỉ “shortlisted”, “hasn't won one yet”.

items.q: How will Rachel pay for the course?
options: in cash on the first day
items.cue: I'll do the transfer this evening
items.explain: Đáp án B: Rachel nói “I'll do the transfer this evening”. A sai vì “we can't take card payments over the phone”; C sai vì cô ấy “I'd rather not carry that much cash around”.

listening.title: Shore Keepers coastal clean-up
listening.titleVi: Chương trình dọn dẹp bờ biển
listening.context: A local radio presenter interviews a volunteer coordinator about a beach clean-up programme.

script.say: Part 2. You will hear a volunteer coordinator talking on local radio about a coastal clean-up programme. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 13.

script.t: Good morning. Joining me in the studio is Helen Marsh, who coordinates the Shore Keepers programme here on the Westcombe coast. Welcome, Helen.
Thanks for having me.
For listeners who haven't come across you before, what exactly does Shore Keepers do?
Put simply, we organise volunteers to clear rubbish from our local beaches. But it's also about getting people to notice what ends up in the sea.
And how did it all begin?
So, a lot of people assume Shore Keepers began because tourists complained about the state of the beaches.
And we did get a few letters from visitors, that's true. But what really got us going was the huge storm three winters ago.
It left the whole of Pebble Bay covered in plastic, and a handful of us just went down with bin bags the next morning.
In that first year we had about forty regulars. These days there are over three hundred people on our mailing list.
Of course, not everyone comes every time. On a typical clean-up day, around a hundred and twenty people turn up, which is fantastic.
Now, people keep asking what's changed this year. Well, we're still working on the same four beaches, and we still meet on Saturdays.
The big new thing is that we're asking everyone to record what they pick up, using a simple app on their phone.
That way the council can see exactly where the rubbish is coming from – fishing gear, takeaway packaging, and so on.
It only takes a few seconds per item, and last month alone we logged nearly nine thousand pieces of litter.
That is a staggering number.

script.say: Now look at questions 14 to 17.

script.t: Let me run through this month's schedule, because each beach is a bit different.
All sessions run from ten until one, and you can come for an hour or stay for the whole morning – whatever suits you.
We start on the 8th at Pebble Bay. There's a big car park at the top, so getting there is easy.
But there's a steep path down to the sand, and it gets slippery, so please wear proper shoes.
On the 15th we're at Gull Point. Parking's fine there too. It's part of a nature reserve, though, so please leave your dogs at home.
They disturb the seabirds, even on a lead.
Then on the 22nd it's Sandown Cove. That's the easiest of the four – it's flat and sheltered.
So it's ideal if you want to bring the kids along. Under twelves just need to stay with an adult.
And finally, on the 29th, Harbour Beach. The car park there is closed for repairs, so I'm afraid there's nowhere to leave a car.
And the buses don't go that way on Saturdays, so walk or cycle if you can. The toilets are open, at least!

script.say: Now look at questions 18 to 20.

script.t: What about equipment and safety? What should people know before they come?
We hand out gloves, sacks and litter pickers at the start, so you don't need to buy anything. Wellington boots aren't necessary either.
But you will need sun cream and a hat. Even in autumn, the sun reflecting off the water is surprisingly strong.
Our safety rules are pretty simple. First, never pick up needles or broken glass yourself.
Mark the spot with a stick and tell a team leader – they have special containers for that.
Second, stay away from the rocks at the far end of each beach. They look solid, but they're covered in weed.
And finally, always check the tide times. The team leader announces them when we start.
When you hear the whistle, everyone moves back up the beach – no exceptions.
And what happens to everything you collect?
Anything that can be recycled goes to the depot in Westcombe. Old fishing nets are sent to a company that turns them into furniture, which people love hearing about.
There's no need to register in advance. Just turn up at the meeting point on the day, and sign in with your team leader.
Helen Marsh, thank you. If you want to join, details are on our website.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: What was the main reason the Shore Keepers programme started?
options: A storm left a beach covered in rubbish.
A local school asked for help.
items.cue: what really got us going was the huge storm
items.explain: Đáp án A: “what really got us going was the huge storm three winters ago”, khiến Pebble Bay “covered in plastic”. C là bẫy: có vài thư phàn nàn của du khách nhưng không phải lý do chính; B không được nhắc đến.

items.q: How many volunteers usually attend each clean-up?
items.cue: around a hundred and twenty people turn up
items.explain: Đáp án B: “On a typical clean-up day, around a hundred and twenty people turn up”. Bẫy: 40 là số người năm đầu, 300 là số người trong “mailing list”, không phải số người thường đến.

items.q: What is new about the programme this year?
options: Clean-ups take place on more beaches.
items.cue: record what they pick up
items.explain: Đáp án C: điểm mới là “we're asking everyone to record what they pick up” bằng ứng dụng điện thoại. A và B sai vì vẫn “the same four beaches” và vẫn họp “on Saturdays”.

groups.instr: What does Helen say about each beach? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 14–17.
options: A can be reached by bus

items.cue: there's a steep path down to the sand
items.explain: Pebble Bay có bãi đỗ xe lớn, nhưng “there's a steep path down to the sand, and it gets slippery” → F (lối đi khó). Không chọn B vì ở đây đỗ xe dễ dàng.

items.cue: please leave your dogs at home
items.explain: Gull Point thuộc khu bảo tồn nên “please leave your dogs at home” → C (không cho mang chó). Đỗ xe ở đây vẫn ổn (“Parking's fine there too”), nên không chọn B.

items.cue: ideal if you want to bring the kids along
items.explain: Sandown Cove bằng phẳng, kín gió, “ideal if you want to bring the kids along” → D (phù hợp cho trẻ em). “kids” được diễn đạt lại thành “children” trong đáp án.

items.cue: there's nowhere to leave a car
items.explain: Harbour Beach: bãi đỗ xe đóng cửa sửa chữa, “there's nowhere to leave a car” → B. Bẫy: A sai vì “the buses don't go that way on Saturdays”; E sai vì “The toilets are open”.

groups.title: Equipment and safety
groups.instr: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.text: Volunteers should bring sun cream and a ___
items.cue: you will need sun cream and a hat
items.explain: Găng tay, bao, que gắp rác đều được phát, ủng cũng không cần, nhưng “you will need sun cream and a hat” → hat. Đề viết “should bring”, bài nói “you will need”.

items.text: Do not touch ___ or broken glass – tell a team leader
items.cue: never pick up needles or broken glass
items.explain: Quy tắc an toàn đầu tiên: “never pick up needles or broken glass yourself” → needles. “Do not touch” trong đề là cách diễn đạt lại của “never pick up”.

items.text: Always check the ___ times before working near the water
items.cue: always check the tide times
items.explain: Quy tắc cuối cùng: “always check the tide times” → tide. Trưởng nhóm sẽ thông báo giờ thủy triều khi bắt đầu buổi dọn dẹp.

listening.title: Feedback on a presentation about bicycles
listening.titleVi: Nhận xét bài thuyết trình về lịch sử xe đạp
listening.context: A tutor gives a student feedback on her presentation about the history of bicycles and urban transport.

script.say: Part 3. You will hear a tutor and a student, Chloe, discussing her presentation on the history of bicycles. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.

script.t: Come in, Chloe. So, I wanted to go over your presentation from Tuesday before you start the written report.
Thanks. I was pretty nervous, so I'm not sure how it came across.
Honestly, it went well. Your old photographs were lovely, and the timeline was clear, but neither of those was what really stood out.
It was the way you opened – with that statistic about factory workers commuting by bike in the 1930s. That grabbed everyone's attention immediately.
Oh good. I almost cut that bit.
Well, I'm glad you didn't. It gave the audience a reason to care about the rest of the talk.
I found it in an old newspaper archive, actually. It took ages, but it felt worth it.
Did you have any particular difficulties preparing it?
Not with the research, really – the library had loads of material. And the slide software was fine.
My real problem was on the day. I was given twelve minutes and I think I took nearly sixteen.
Yes, I noticed. That's something to practise. Now, the section on the safety bicycle.
I did rehearse, but only in my head. I think when you're actually speaking, everything takes longer.
That's very common. Next time, try a full run-through out loud with a timer, and decide in advance which slides you can skip if you're behind.
That's a good tip. I'll do that.
You explained the chain drive and the equal-sized wheels very thoroughly. Perhaps a little too thoroughly.
What was missing was why it mattered for cities – that ordinary workers could suddenly live further from the factory, for example.
Right, I see. I got a bit carried away with the engineering side.
And then you talked about the decline of cycling after the war. What was your main argument there?
Well, most people say it was simply because cars got cheaper. And that's part of it.
But the sources I read argued that the bigger factor was that planners redesigned streets around motor traffic, so cycling just felt dangerous.
Good – that's a more interesting point, and you should make it more strongly.
Some of the audience didn't quite follow it, because it came right at the end when you were rushing.
Yeah, that's true. I'll give it more space in the report, and maybe use an example from a particular city.

script.say: Now look at questions 25 and 26.

script.t: So what should I change for the written version?
Two things. First, I'd add a comparison. Look at how the Netherlands handled the same pressures – they made very different choices.
I was also thinking of interviewing some local cyclists.
It's a nice idea, but you'd need ethics approval, and there simply isn't time before the deadline.
Maybe save that for your dissertation next year.
OK. Should I put in more maps?
No, you've got plenty of maps. But your figures stop around 2010. You should update them with something more recent.
Fair enough. And the introduction's OK as it is?
The introduction's fine. Leave it.

script.say: Now look at questions 27 to 30.

script.t: Let's talk about your sources. What are you planning to do with each one?
Well, the transport museum website – some of its numbers don't match the books I used, so I'm going to double-check its figures.
Sensible. And the 1972 government report?
That's really my strongest source, so I'll build the main argument around it.
Good. What about the cycling club newsletter?
I thought about asking the librarian if there were other issues, but honestly, it's quite one-sided. I'm going to take it out altogether.
I think that's wise. And the documentary film?
It quoted a historian, Dr Weber, so I'm going to track down the article she originally wrote, instead of relying on the film.
Excellent. Always better to go back to the original. Right, I think you're in good shape.
When is the report due, exactly? I wrote down two different dates.
It's the end of next month. Send me a draft of the comparison section a week before, if you like, and I'll give you some quick comments.
That would be really helpful. Thanks so much, Dr Ellis.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: What did the tutor think was the most effective part of the presentation?
items.cue: It was the way you opened
items.explain: Đáp án B: thầy khen ảnh và dòng thời gian nhưng nói “neither of those was what really stood out”; điểm nổi bật là “the way you opened – with that statistic”. A và C bị loại rõ ràng.

items.q: What difficulty did Chloe have?
items.cue: I was given twelve minutes
items.explain: Đáp án B: “I was given twelve minutes and I think I took nearly sixteen” → vượt thời gian. A sai vì thư viện “had loads of material”; C sai vì “the slide software was fine”.

items.q: The tutor says the section on the safety bicycle needed
options: a clearer link to city life.
items.cue: why it mattered for cities
items.explain: Đáp án B: thầy nói điều còn thiếu là “why it mattered for cities”. A sai vì phần kỹ thuật đã giải thích “Perhaps a little too thoroughly”; C (ngày tháng) không được nhắc đến.

items.q: According to Chloe, the main reason cycling declined was that
items.cue: planners redesigned streets around motor traffic
items.explain: Đáp án B: theo nguồn Chloe đọc, yếu tố lớn hơn là “planners redesigned streets around motor traffic”. A là bẫy: xe hơi rẻ hơn chỉ là “part of it”; C không được nhắc đến.

groups.instr: Choose TWO letters, A–E.
groups.q: Which TWO changes does the tutor recommend for the written report?
options: A add a comparison with another country
groups.cue: update them with something more recent
groups.explain: Đáp án A và E: thầy khuyên “add a comparison” với Hà Lan và cập nhật số liệu “with something more recent”. B sai vì cần phê duyệt đạo đức, không kịp; C sai vì “you've got plenty of maps”; D sai vì “The introduction's fine”.

groups.instr: What does Chloe plan to do with each source? Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 27–30.
options: A use it as the main evidence
D quote it in the introduction
F ask the librarian about it

items.cue: double-check its figures
items.explain: Với website bảo tàng giao thông, số liệu không khớp sách nên “I'm going to double-check its figures” → B (kiểm tra số liệu).

items.cue: I'll build the main argument around it
items.explain: Báo cáo chính phủ năm 1972 là “my strongest source, so I'll build the main argument around it” → A (dùng làm bằng chứng chính).

items.cue: take it out altogether
items.explain: Bẫy: Chloe có nghĩ tới việc “asking the librarian” (phương án F) nhưng vì bản tin quá phiến diện nên “I'm going to take it out altogether” → C (loại bỏ).

items.cue: track down the article she originally wrote
items.explain: Phim tài liệu trích lời Dr Weber, nên Chloe sẽ “track down the article she originally wrote, instead of relying on the film” → E (tìm bài viết gốc).

listening.title: Sleep and memory in teenagers
listening.titleVi: Giấc ngủ và trí nhớ ở tuổi thiếu niên
listening.context: A university lecture on how sleep affects memory consolidation in teenagers.

script.say: Part 4. You will hear a lecture about sleep and memory in teenagers. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

script.t: Good afternoon, everyone. Today we're looking at something that affects every one of you: sleep, and in particular how it shapes memory in adolescence.
I'll start with the basic process, then look at what's different about teenagers, then a recent study, and finally what all this means in practice.
So, first, memory consolidation. That's the process by which fragile, short-term memories become stable, long-term ones.
For a long time, sleep was seen as a passive state – the brain simply switching off. We now know that's wrong.
In fact, some areas of the brain are almost as active during certain stages of sleep as they are when we're awake.
During sleep, the brain essentially replays the day's experiences, running through the same patterns of activity again and again.
The key structure here is the hippocampus, a small, curved region deep in the brain.
You can think of it as a temporary store, a kind of inbox, where new information is held for a short time.
Then, during deep sleep, that information is gradually transferred to the cortex, the outer layer of the brain, for long-term storage.
What about REM sleep, the stage when we dream? Its role is less clear. It doesn't seem to be essential for storing facts.
But it may help with creative thinking – making unexpected connections between ideas we already have.
In several experiments, people who'd had a period of REM sleep were better at solving puzzles that needed a fresh approach.
OK, so why are teenagers a special case? Well, it's not simply that they're lazy, whatever their parents might say.
At puberty, the body clock shifts. In particular, the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy, is delayed by up to two hours.
Screens and phone use make this worse, but they're not the root cause. The shift is biological.
The result is that a typical sixteen-year-old simply isn't tired at ten o'clock, yet still has to get up at six thirty for school.
Over a week, that builds up into what researchers call sleep debt, and it's very hard to pay back at the weekend.
And how much sleep do teenagers actually need? Many parents believe seven hours is enough.
In fact, the research suggests roughly nine hours a night – and very few teenagers get anywhere near that during the school week.
Let's turn now to a study I want to describe in some detail. Researchers worked with two hundred students aged fifteen to seventeen.
Each student learned forty words from an invented language – invented, so that nobody could have seen the words before.
Half of them learned the words in the evening and then slept. The other half learned them in the morning and stayed awake all day.
Importantly, both groups had the same amount of time to study, and they used exactly the same materials.
Twelve hours later, both groups were tested. The early analysis suggested the sleep group remembered about thirty percent more.
But once the researchers removed students who'd reported being ill, the difference settled at twenty percent. Still a very substantial effect.
The researchers also found that the benefit was greatest for the words students had found most difficult during learning.
In other words, sleep seemed to help most with the information that was weakest to begin with.
So, finally, what are the practical implications?
At the level of policy, several districts have experimented with starting the school day later, around eight thirty instead of seven thirty.
Schools that made the change generally reported fewer absences, and in some cases, modest improvements in grades.
There were concerns that students would just go to bed later, but most of the data shows they actually gained around forty minutes of sleep.
Of course, a later start creates problems too, with buses, sports schedules and parents' working hours, so it isn't an easy decision.
And for individual students, the message is simple. Probably the worst thing you can do before an exam is late-night cramming.
You may feel you're gaining time, but you're cutting out the very sleep your brain needs to keep what you've studied.
A far better strategy is to spread your revision over several days, and let each night of sleep do some of the work for you.
Right. Next week we'll look at how exercise affects attention.

groups.title: Sleep and memory consolidation in teenagers
groups.instr: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.text: Memory consolidation: during sleep the brain ___ the day’s experiences
items.cue: the brain essentially replays the day's experiences
items.explain: Giảng viên nói “the brain essentially replays the day's experiences” → replays. Cần giữ đúng dạng động từ có “-s” cho khớp ngữ pháp câu.

items.text: The ___ acts as a temporary store for new information
items.cue: The key structure here is the hippocampus
items.explain: “The key structure here is the hippocampus”, được ví như “a temporary store, a kind of inbox” → hippocampus. Cần viết đúng chính tả.

items.text: In deep sleep, information moves to the ___ for long-term storage
items.cue: gradually transferred to the cortex
items.explain: Trong giấc ngủ sâu, thông tin “is gradually transferred to the cortex” để lưu trữ lâu dài → cortex. “moves to” trong đề là cách diễn đạt lại “transferred to”.

items.cue: it may help with creative thinking
items.explain: Vai trò của REM chưa rõ, không thiết yếu cho việc lưu dữ kiện, nhưng “it may help with creative thinking” → creative.

items.text: Teenagers: release of the hormone ___ is delayed
items.cue: the release of melatonin
items.explain: Ở tuổi dậy thì, “the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy, is delayed by up to two hours” → melatonin.

items.text: Teenagers need about ___ hours of sleep per night
items.cue: roughly nine hours a night
items.explain: Bẫy: nhiều phụ huynh tin “seven hours is enough”, nhưng nghiên cứu cho thấy “roughly nine hours a night” → nine/9. “about” trong đề tương ứng “roughly”.

items.text: Study: students learned forty words from an invented ___
items.cue: forty words from an invented language
items.explain: Học sinh học “forty words from an invented language” → language. Lý do dùng ngôn ngữ tự tạo: để không ai từng gặp các từ đó trước.

items.text: The sleep group remembered ___ percent more words
items.cue: the difference settled at twenty percent
items.explain: Bẫy số: phân tích ban đầu là “about thirty percent more”, nhưng sau khi loại học sinh bị ốm thì “the difference settled at twenty percent” → twenty/20.

items.cue: reported fewer absences
items.explain: Các trường bắt đầu muộn hơn “generally reported fewer absences” → absences. Không chọn “grades” vì bài nói điểm số chỉ cải thiện nhẹ, không phải “fewer”.

items.text: Students should avoid late-night ___ before exams
items.cue: late-night cramming
items.explain: “Probably the worst thing you can do before an exam is late-night cramming” → cramming. Đề dùng “avoid”, tương ứng với ý “the worst thing you can do”.

listening.title: Arranging a homestay
listening.titleVi: Sắp xếp chỗ ở homestay cho du học sinh
listening.context: A British student phones a homestay agency in Australia to arrange accommodation.

script.say: Part 1. You will hear a student phoning a homestay agency to arrange accommodation. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.

script.t: Good morning, Southern Cross Homestays, Bree speaking. How can I help you?
Hi there. I'm a student coming over from the UK next month, and I'm hoping to arrange a homestay for when I arrive.
Lovely, you've come to the right place. I'll just pop your details into our system. Can I take your name?
Sure. It's Callum Ashworth.
And how do you spell your surname, Callum?
It's A, S, H, W, O, R, T, H.
Great, thanks. And when are you planning to arrive?
My flight lands on the 21st of February.
Actually, hang on – I changed my booking last week. It's the 23rd now, not the 21st.
No worries. The 23rd of February. And what will you be studying while you're here?
I've got a place on an exchange programme at Harbourside Institute. I'm doing architecture.
Oh, nice. We get a lot of engineering students from there, but not many architects. How long is the programme?
The course itself is twelve weeks, but I'm going travelling for the last two.
So I'll only need somewhere to stay for the first part.
OK, so ten weeks of accommodation. Now, do you have any dietary requirements? Our families like to know in advance.
I eat pretty much everything. I'm not vegetarian or anything like that.
The only thing is I'm allergic to nuts, so that's quite important.
Absolutely, I'll put that in capital letters. And what sort of budget are you working with? Our prices include meals.
The website said homestays start at two hundred and fifty dollars a week.
That's right, but that's for a shared bathroom and breakfast only.
I'd really like dinner included as well, so I can go up to two hundred and ninety dollars a week. That's my absolute limit, though.
Two hundred and ninety. That gives us plenty of options.

script.say: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.

script.t: OK, Callum, I've got two families who I think would suit you really well. The first are the Morrisons.
They live in Glenfield, which is a quiet suburb in the north of the city.
How far is that from the institute?
It's about twenty minutes by train, but the station's quite a long walk from the house.
So most of our students take the bus instead, which goes straight there. That takes thirty-five minutes.
That's not too bad. I can read on the bus. What's the house like?
It's quite big, with a lovely garden. The best thing is that the guest room has its own bathroom, so you wouldn't have to share.
Oh, that would be nice. Do they have kids?
Their children have grown up and left home, so it's just the two of them now. Very relaxed.
The second option is the Delaneys. They're a young family with two little girls, and they live much closer to the institute.
Close enough to walk?
Well, it's about forty minutes on foot, so that's a bit far every day.
But they'll lend you a bicycle for free, and there's a cycle path nearly all the way.
Great, I cycle everywhere at home anyway.
Do they have any pets? I'm fine with animals, but I'd like to know.
They used to have a dog, but sadly he died last year. Now they've just got a parrot. Apparently he talks a lot!
Ha, that sounds fun. I think I'd like to find out more about the Delaneys first, if that's possible.
Of course. I'll email you their profile this afternoon and set up a video call for later in the week.
Brilliant. Thanks so much for your help, Bree.
My pleasure, Callum. Talk soon.

groups.title: Southern Cross Homestays – Student details
groups.instr: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.cue: A, S, H, W, O, R, T, H
items.explain: Callum đánh vần họ của mình: “A, S, H, W, O, R, T, H”, nên đáp án là Ashworth. Chú ý viết đúng từng chữ cái, đặc biệt cụm “SH” và “TH”.

items.cue: It's the 23rd now
items.explain: Bẫy đổi thông tin: ban đầu Callum nói “the 21st of February”, sau đó sửa lại “It's the 23rd now, not the 21st”. Đáp án là 23, không phải 21.

items.cue: I'm doing architecture
items.explain: Callum nói “I'm doing architecture”. Bẫy: Bree nhắc đến “engineering students” nhưng đó là sinh viên khác, không phải ngành của Callum.

items.cue: so ten weeks of accommodation
items.explain: Khóa học dài “twelve weeks” nhưng Callum đi du lịch “for the last two”, nên Bree chốt “so ten weeks of accommodation”. Đáp án là 10, không phải 12.

items.cue: I'm allergic to nuts
items.explain: Callum nói “I'm allergic to nuts”. Câu trước “I'm not vegetarian” là thông tin gây nhiễu, không phải dị ứng.

items.cue: two hundred and ninety dollars a week
items.explain: Mức “two hundred and fifty dollars a week” chỉ là giá khởi điểm trên website; Callum nói “I can go up to two hundred and ninety dollars a week. That's my absolute limit”, nên ngân sách tối đa là 290.

groups.title: Possible homestay families
groups.instr: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.text: The Morrisons (Glenfield) – journey to institute: ___ minutes by bus
items.cue: That takes thirty-five minutes.
items.explain: Đi tàu mất “about twenty minutes” nhưng ga xa nhà nên sinh viên thường đi xe buýt: “That takes thirty-five minutes”. Đáp án là 35, không phải 20.

items.text: The Morrisons – special feature: guest room has its own ___
items.cue: has its own bathroom
items.explain: Bree nói “the guest room has its own bathroom, so you wouldn't have to share”. “Lovely garden” cũng được nhắc nhưng không phải đặc điểm của phòng khách.

items.text: The Delaneys – journey to institute: by ___ (lent free of charge)
items.cue: they'll lend you a bicycle for free
items.explain: Đi bộ mất “about forty minutes”, quá xa, nhưng gia đình “they'll lend you a bicycle for free”; “for free” tương ứng với “lent free of charge” trong đề.

items.cue: they've just got a parrot
items.explain: Bẫy: họ từng nuôi chó nhưng “he died last year”; hiện tại “Now they've just got a parrot”. Đáp án là parrot, không phải dog.

listening.title: Volunteering at a science festival
listening.titleVi: Tình nguyện viên tại lễ hội khoa học
listening.context: A manager gives a briefing to new volunteers at a city science festival.

script.say: Part 2. You will hear a manager talking to a group of new volunteers at a science festival. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.

script.t: Hi everyone, and thanks so much for coming in this early. I'm Rosa, and I'm the volunteer manager for the Eastport Science Festival.
This is the festival's eighth year, and we're expecting around forty thousand visitors over the weekend, so we really do need you.
I'll start with a few practical points, and then I'll run through where the main stalls are, because visitors will ask you about that all day long.
OK, so first, what you'll be getting. Everyone gets a festival T-shirt in bright orange, so people can spot you in the crowd.
Last year we handed out caps as well, but people kept losing them, so this year it's just the T-shirt.
You'll also each receive a voucher for lunch at any of the food trucks, which you can use on either day.
A few of you asked about parking. Unfortunately we can't offer that, because the main car park is being used for the event itself.
The bus company is running extra services all weekend, though, and if you show your volunteer badge, the ride is free.
Now, your duties. A lot of you probably think you'll be checking tickets, but that's actually done by our security staff.
And the festival maps won't be delivered by the printers until Saturday lunchtime, so you won't be giving those out in the morning either.
So on Saturday morning, your main job is helping exhibitors unpack and set up their stalls. Some of the equipment is heavy, so please work in pairs.
Next, something really important: lost children. With this many families, it will happen, probably more than once.
If a child comes to you and can't find their parents, please don't walk them over to the information tent yourself.
Parents usually come back to the place where they last saw their child. So stay exactly where you are with the child and radio the control room.
They'll make an announcement and send someone to you. Never, ever leave the child alone, even for a minute.
Each pair will have one radio. Please test it as soon as you get it, and keep it switched to channel four, which goes straight to the control room.
You'll each get two breaks of twenty minutes a day. Just let your team leader know before you go, so nobody's left on their own.
Finally, a few people have asked what's different this year. Some of you may have heard the festival is longer, but it isn't – it's still two days.
Entry is free for under-sixteens, but then, it always has been. The big change is that, after all the rain last year, we've moved a lot of events indoors.

script.say: Now look at questions 15 to 20.

script.t: OK, let's look at where things are. If you take the map in your welcome pack, you'll see the festival is spread across the old town.
We'll start with robot football, which is always one of the most popular events. That's in the east marquee – the big white tent by the bridge.
Then there's telescope viewing. People often expect that to be on the riverside lawn, because it's so open.
But the trees there block too much of the sky, so it's on the library steps, which face south.
The slime laboratory is very popular with younger kids, and very messy. It's in the Old Fire Station, where the floors are easy to hose down.
At two o'clock each day, the weather balloon will go up from the riverside lawn. Please help keep people back from the launch area.
The balloon carries a small camera, and the pictures it takes will be shown on the big screen later, so it's worth telling visitors about that.
For anyone interested in dinosaurs, and that's usually everyone under ten, the fossil dig is in the museum courtyard. It's a sandpit with real fossil copies buried in it.
And last, the brain puzzle tables. These were originally going to be in the market square.
But the city council needs that space for bike parking, so they've moved into the town hall foyer, just inside the main doors.
Right, that's everything. Grab a coffee, find your partner, and I'll see you at your stations in fifteen minutes.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: What will each volunteer be given?
items.cue: a voucher for lunch
items.explain: Rosa nói “You'll also each receive a voucher for lunch” (voucher for lunch = meal voucher). A sai vì năm nay không phát mũ nữa: “this year it's just the T-shirt”; C sai vì “we can't offer” chỗ đỗ xe.

items.q: On Saturday morning, volunteers will mainly be
items.cue: helping exhibitors unpack and set up their stalls
items.explain: “your main job is helping exhibitors unpack and set up their stalls” tương ứng với “helping exhibitors prepare”. A sai vì soát vé do “our security staff” làm; B sai vì bản đồ đến trưa thứ Bảy mới được giao.

items.q: If volunteers find a lost child, they should
options: take the child to the information tent.
remain in the same place and contact the control room.
items.cue: stay exactly where you are with the child
items.explain: Rosa dặn “stay exactly where you are with the child and radio the control room”. B sai vì “please don't walk them over to the information tent”; C sai vì phòng điều khiển “They'll make an announcement”, không phải tình nguyện viên.

items.q: What is new about the festival this year?
items.cue: we've moved a lot of events indoors
items.explain: “The big change is that... we've moved a lot of events indoors” (indoors = inside). A sai: “it isn't – it's still two days”; C sai vì miễn phí cho trẻ em không phải điều mới: “it always has been”.

groups.instr: Where is each of the following stalls located? Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to questions 15–20.

items.cue: That's in the east marquee
items.explain: Rosa nói robot football “That's in the east marquee – the big white tent by the bridge”. Đáp án là E.

items.cue: it's on the library steps
items.explain: Bẫy: nhiều người tưởng ngắm sao ở “riverside lawn” nhưng cây cối che trời, nên “it's on the library steps”. Đáp án là C, không phải B.

items.cue: It's in the Old Fire Station
items.explain: Phòng thí nghiệm slime rất bẩn nên đặt ở nơi dễ xịt rửa sàn: “It's in the Old Fire Station”. Đáp án là G.

items.cue: the weather balloon will go up from the riverside lawn
items.explain: “the weather balloon will go up from the riverside lawn” (go up = launch). Đáp án là B; riverside lawn bị loại ở câu 16 nhưng là đáp án đúng ở câu này.

items.cue: the fossil dig is in the museum courtyard
items.explain: Rosa nói “the fossil dig is in the museum courtyard”. Đáp án là D.

items.cue: they've moved into the town hall foyer
items.explain: Bẫy: ban đầu định đặt ở “the market square” nhưng hội đồng thành phố cần chỗ để xe đạp, nên “they've moved into the town hall foyer”. Đáp án là A, không phải F.

listening.title: Remote working and productivity
listening.titleVi: Làm việc từ xa và năng suất – thảo luận tình huống
listening.context: Two students discuss their case study on remote working with their lecturer.

script.say: Part 3. You will hear two students, Priya and Leo, discussing their case study with their lecturer, Dr Halvorsen. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.

script.t: Come in, both of you. So, you're doing your case study on remote working at Fernvale Analytics. Remind me why you picked that company.
Well, my cousin works there, so I'd heard a bit about it. But that wasn't really the reason.
No, the main thing was that the company published really detailed data about the switch – hours, output, staff surveys, everything.
Most firms just put out a press release saying everyone loves working from home.
Fair enough. That's a good reason. Now, I've read your outline, and I do have one concern about how productivity was measured.
You mean the task-tracking system?
Yes. It's not too complicated, and it isn't based on people's own opinions, which is good.
But they simply counted the number of tasks completed each week, and nothing about how good the work was.
So someone could rush through twenty small tasks and look more productive than someone who did one difficult job well.
That's true. We should probably point that out in our evaluation.
We could also mention that the managers chose which tasks went into the system, so some kinds of work weren't counted at all.
Good point. Anything that shows you've thought critically about the evidence will help your mark.
Definitely. What about the findings themselves? Was there anything you didn't expect?
I'd assumed productivity would drop at first, while people got used to it, but it actually stayed pretty steady.
For me, the biggest surprise was that it was the junior employees who were keenest to get back to the office.
I'd always thought young people would want to stay at home, but they said they missed learning from more experienced colleagues.
Several of them said they didn't feel comfortable asking quick questions over a message. It felt like they were interrupting.
That's come up in other studies too, actually. Right, and what problems did staff report?
Some people mentioned bad internet connections, but honestly it was only a handful, and the company paid for upgrades quite quickly.
The biggest complaint was that people couldn't switch off in the evenings, because their laptop was always there on the kitchen table.
And the other big one was the number of video calls. Some managers were scheduling six or seven a day just to check in.
We expected loneliness to be a major issue, but it hardly featured. And everyone was given a laptop and a proper chair, so equipment wasn't a problem.

script.say: Now look at questions 26 to 30.

script.t: OK, let's go through the sections of your presentation. You've got a section on the company background first.
Yes, we go through its history since it was founded in 1998.
Nobody really needs all of that. Cut it down to a minute and get to the interesting part sooner.
OK. Then we have the survey results. At the moment it's mostly a long list of percentages.
I was thinking we could add even more statistics, to make it more convincing.
I'd say you've got enough numbers already. The problem is they're hard to follow when they're read out. Show them as a chart instead.
Would a table work? We've already got one in the written report.
Keep the table in the report, by all means. But on a slide, a bar chart is much quicker for an audience to take in.
Right. Next is the section on how they redesigned the office for people coming back in.
That part feels a bit dry. You did some staff interviews, didn't you? Use some of the comments from the interviews to bring it to life.
Good idea. After that, there's the four-day week trial they ran last year.
That's fascinating, but one company on its own doesn't tell us much. I'd compare it with another company that's tried the same thing.
And finally we have the limitations of the study. At the moment that comes in the middle.
It interrupts the flow there. Put the limitations at the end, just before your conclusion.
OK, that all makes sense. Thanks, Dr Halvorsen.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

items.q: Why did the students choose Fernvale Analytics for their case study?
options: It is a very well-known company.
It made a lot of information available.
A relative of Leo works there.
items.cue: the company published really detailed data
items.explain: Priya nói “the main thing was that the company published really detailed data” (published data = made information available). A sai vì Leo nói họ hàng làm ở đó “wasn't really the reason”; B không được nhắc đến.

items.q: What is the lecturer's concern about the way productivity was measured?
options: It ignored the quality of work.
items.cue: nothing about how good the work was
items.explain: Giảng viên nói hệ thống chỉ đếm số việc hoàn thành “and nothing about how good the work was” (how good = quality). B và C sai vì ông khẳng định “It's not too complicated, and it isn't based on people's own opinions”.

items.q: What surprised Priya about the findings?
options: Younger staff wanted to return to the office.
Productivity fell in the first few weeks.
items.cue: the junior employees who were keenest to get back to the office
items.explain: Priya nói “the biggest surprise was that it was the junior employees who were keenest to get back to the office” (junior = younger, get back = return). A là dự đoán của Leo và thực tế năng suất “stayed pretty steady”; C không được nhắc.

groups.instr: Choose TWO letters, A–E.
groups.q: Which TWO problems did many employees report?
options: B difficulty switching off from work
E a lack of suitable equipment
groups.cue: people couldn't switch off in the evenings
groups.explain: B và D: “The biggest complaint was that people couldn't switch off” và “the number of video calls... six or seven a day” (video calls = online meetings). A chỉ “only a handful”; C “hardly featured”; E sai vì “equipment wasn't a problem”.

groups.instr: What does the lecturer suggest for each section of the presentation? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 26–30.
options: E compare it with another organisation
F move it to a later point

items.cue: Cut it down to a minute
items.explain: Về lịch sử công ty, giảng viên nói “Cut it down to a minute” (cut down = make shorter). Đáp án là A.

items.cue: Show them as a chart instead
items.explain: Leo muốn thêm số liệu nhưng giảng viên bác bỏ: “you've got enough numbers already... Show them as a chart instead” (chart = present visually). Đáp án là D, không phải B.

items.cue: Use some of the comments from the interviews
items.explain: Phần thiết kế lại văn phòng “feels a bit dry”, nên giảng viên khuyên “Use some of the comments from the interviews” (staff interviews = comments from employees). Đáp án là C.

items.cue: compare it with another company that's tried the same thing
items.explain: Giảng viên nói “I'd compare it with another company that's tried the same thing” (company = organisation). Đáp án là E.

items.cue: Put the limitations at the end
items.explain: Phần hạn chế đang nằm ở giữa, giảng viên bảo “Put the limitations at the end, just before your conclusion” (at the end = a later point). Đáp án là F.

thư giãn, ngắt kết nối với công việc
hỏi han, cập nhật tình hình
