Until larger and longer-term trials are conducted, the question is likely to be settled as much by political values as by evidence.

questions.q: Support for UBI has come from people with very different political views.
questions.explain: Bài viết: UBI has been "Advocated at different times by radical reformers and free-market economists alike" → TRUE.

questions.q: Pilot projects have shown a sharp fall in employment among recipients.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "most studies have found little evidence of a significant decline in employment" → FALSE.

questions.q: Finland has decided to introduce UBI for its entire population.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nhắc Phần Lan có dự án thí điểm với nhóm chọn lọc, không nói nước này quyết định áp dụng toàn quốc → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What is the "welfare trap"?
options: When people who start paid work lose benefits so quickly that they gain little
When the state stops all payments
When taxes are set too low
questions.explain: Bài viết: people "who take on paid work lose benefits at such a rate that they gain little or nothing financially".

questions.q: Why do sceptics doubt the results of the pilot projects?
options: Temporary experiments cannot show how behaviour or prices would change under a permanent scheme.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "temporary experiments cannot reveal how behaviour or prices might change if a payment were permanent and nationwide".

readings.title: The Slow Pandemic: Antibiotic Resistance
readings.summaryVi: Việc lạm dụng kháng sinh ở người và vật nuôi đẩy nhanh tình trạng vi khuẩn kháng thuốc, trong khi thuốc mới ngày càng ít; cần quản lý kê đơn, chẩn đoán nhanh và mô hình tài trợ mới.
readings.summaryEn: The overuse of antibiotics in people and farm animals speeds up drug resistance in bacteria, while fewer new drugs are being developed; better prescribing, rapid diagnosis and new funding models are needed.
readings.text:
When penicillin entered widespread use in the 1940s, it transformed medicine. Infections that had routinely killed, such as pneumonia, infected wounds and complications of childbirth, suddenly became treatable. Antibiotics also made possible many modern procedures, from major surgery to cancer chemotherapy, which depend on the ability to prevent or control bacterial infection. Yet even Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin, warned that its misuse could render bacteria resistant. That warning has proved remarkably prescient.

Resistance is, at its core, a matter of natural selection. Whenever bacteria are exposed to an antibiotic, the most susceptible are killed, while any that happen to carry a resistance mechanism survive and multiply. Bacteria can also exchange genetic material with one another, allowing resistance to spread between different species. Consequently, every use of an antibiotic, however justified, exerts some selective pressure; unnecessary use simply accelerates the process.

Such unnecessary use is widespread. Antibiotics are frequently prescribed for viral illnesses such as colds and influenza, against which they are entirely ineffective. In some countries they can be purchased without a prescription, and patients who stop a course early or share leftover tablets may contribute further. Agriculture is another major factor: in many parts of the world, large quantities are administered to livestock not to treat disease but to promote growth or to compensate for crowded conditions.

The consequences are already severe. Drug-resistant infections are estimated to be directly responsible for over a million deaths a year, and some strains have emerged that resist almost every available treatment. Compounding the problem, the pipeline of new antibiotics has slowed dramatically. Because new antibiotics would ideally be used sparingly, to preserve their effectiveness, pharmaceutical companies have little prospect of recovering development costs, and many have withdrawn from the field.

Addressing the crisis therefore requires action on several levels. Stewardship programmes in hospitals aim to ensure that antibiotics are prescribed only when necessary and that the right drug is chosen. Rapid diagnostic tests can help clinicians distinguish bacterial from viral infections. Improved sanitation and vaccination reduce the number of infections in the first place. Some governments are experimenting with new funding models, such as paying companies a fixed annual fee for access to a new antibiotic, regardless of how much is sold, thereby separating profit from sales volume.

Because bacteria do not respect borders, no single country can solve the problem alone. Experts describe antimicrobial resistance as a slow-moving pandemic: less visible than a sudden outbreak, but potentially just as dangerous if left unchecked.

questions.q: Alexander Fleming warned that misuse of penicillin could lead to resistance.
questions.explain: Bài viết: Fleming "warned that its misuse could render bacteria resistant" → TRUE.

questions.q: Antibiotics are effective against colds and influenza.
questions.explain: Bài viết: antibiotics are prescribed for colds and influenza, "against which they are entirely ineffective" → FALSE.

questions.q: Most new antibiotics are now developed by universities.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói nhiều công ty dược đã rút khỏi lĩnh vực này, không nhắc đến vai trò của các trường đại học → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why have many pharmaceutical companies withdrawn from developing antibiotics?
options: Antibiotics are too easy to make.
Bacteria no longer cause serious infections.
New antibiotics would be used sparingly, so costs are hard to recover.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Because new antibiotics would ideally be used sparingly", companies "have little prospect of recovering development costs".

questions.q: What is the purpose of paying companies a fixed annual fee?
options: To separate profit from sales volume
questions.explain: Bài viết: the fee is paid "regardless of how much is sold, thereby separating profit from sales volume".

readings.title: Learning in the School Garden
readings.summaryVi: Nhiều trường học có vườn rau nhỏ; học sinh học về thiên nhiên, ăn uống lành mạnh và làm việc nhóm qua việc trồng cây.
readings.summaryEn: Many schools have small vegetable gardens, where students learn about nature, healthy eating and teamwork by growing plants.
readings.text:
In many countries, more and more schools now have a small garden. Children plant seeds, water the plants and pick vegetables when they are ready. For some pupils, it is the first time they have seen how food grows.

Teachers say that a garden is like an outdoor classroom. In science lessons, pupils can watch insects and learn why plants need sun and water. In maths, they measure how tall the plants are each week and draw charts. Even reading and writing lessons can use the garden: children write diaries about what they see.

The garden can also change what children like to eat. Many young people say they do not like vegetables. However, teachers often notice that children are happy to try a carrot or a tomato that they have grown themselves. Some schools use the vegetables in the school kitchen, so the pupils can eat them at lunch.

Working in the garden is a team activity, too. Pupils share jobs, such as watering, digging and taking away weeds, and they must help each other. Quiet children sometimes feel more confident outside than in the classroom.

Of course, a garden needs care during the summer holidays, when the school is closed. In some schools, families take turns to visit and water the plants. Without this help, many of the plants would die before the new school year starts.

questions.q: Some children see how food grows for the first time in a school garden.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "For some pupils, it is the first time they have seen how food grows" → TRUE.

questions.q: Pupils use the garden only in science lessons.
questions.explain: Khu vườn được dùng cả trong giờ toán (đo chiều cao cây, vẽ biểu đồ) và giờ đọc – viết (viết nhật ký), không chỉ môn khoa học → FALSE.

questions.q: Schools with gardens get better exam results.
questions.explain: Bài viết không nhắc đến kết quả thi của học sinh → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What do teachers often notice about children and vegetables?
options: They refuse to eat any vegetables at school.
They are happy to try vegetables they grew themselves.
They prefer vegetables from the supermarket.
They only like carrots and tomatoes.
questions.explain: Bài viết: giáo viên nhận thấy trẻ "happy to try a carrot or a tomato that they have grown themselves".

questions.q: How do some schools look after the garden in the summer holidays?
options: They close the garden until autumn.
Teachers stay at school every day.
Families take turns to water the plants.
They pay a gardener to do the work.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "families take turns to visit and water the plants" – các gia đình thay phiên nhau tưới cây.

readings.title: What Do Libraries Do Today?
readings.summaryVi: Thư viện ngày nay không chỉ cho mượn sách mà còn có máy tính, lớp học, hoạt động cho trẻ em và là nơi gặp gỡ miễn phí của cộng đồng.
readings.summaryEn: Libraries today do more than lend books: they offer computers, classes and activities for children, and they are a free meeting place for the community.
readings.text:
Some people think that libraries are not important any more. After all, we can read the news, find information and even borrow e-books on our phones. But in many towns, the local library is busier than ever. So what do people do there?

Of course, people still go to the library to borrow books. Borrowing is usually free, and you can take home books, magazines, films and sometimes even games. If the library does not have the book you want, the staff can often order it from another library.

But libraries are not only about books. Most libraries have computers and free internet, which is very useful for people who do not have these at home. Some people use them to look for jobs or to fill in forms for the government. Library staff can help people who are not confident with technology.

Libraries also offer many activities. There are story times for small children, homework clubs for school pupils and language classes for adults. Some libraries lend tools or musical instruments, and a few even have rooms where people can use 3D printers.

Finally, a library is one of the few places in a town where you can sit inside for a long time without paying anything. Students come to study in a quiet place, and older people come to read the newspaper and meet friends. For many people, the library is an important part of community life.

questions.q: Many local libraries are now busier than before.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "in many towns, the local library is busier than ever" → TRUE.

questions.q: Library staff can sometimes get books from other libraries.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the staff can often order it from another library" → TRUE.

questions.q: Most libraries charge money for using the internet.
questions.explain: Bài viết nói hầu hết thư viện có "computers and free internet" – internet miễn phí → FALSE.

questions.q: Which activity for adults is mentioned in the text?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "language classes for adults". Story times dành cho trẻ nhỏ; nấu ăn và thể thao không được nhắc đến.

questions.q: According to the last paragraph, why is a library special?
options: It is open twenty-four hours a day.
People can stay there for a long time without paying.
It is the biggest building in town.
questions.explain: Bài viết: thư viện là một trong số ít nơi "where you can sit inside for a long time without paying anything".

readings.title: The Power of a Daily Walk
readings.summaryVi: Đi bộ mỗi ngày là cách vận động đơn giản, miễn phí, tốt cho tim, tâm trạng và giấc ngủ; bài viết gợi ý cách biến đi bộ thành thói quen.
readings.summaryEn: Walking every day is a simple, free form of exercise that is good for the heart, mood and sleep; the article suggests ways to make walking a habit.
readings.text:
Many people want to be healthier, but they do not have time or money for a gym. Doctors often say that one of the best kinds of exercise is also one of the easiest: walking.

Walking is good for the heart, and it helps to keep a healthy weight. Health organisations usually advise adults to do at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise every week. A brisk walk of about 30 minutes on five days a week is one simple way to reach this goal. 'Brisk' means that you walk fast enough to breathe a little harder, but you can still talk.

Walking is good for the mind, too. People who walk regularly often say that they feel calmer and less stressed. Walking outside in daylight may also help you to sleep better at night.

It is easy to make walking part of your day. You can get off the bus one stop early, take the stairs instead of the lift, or walk with a friend or colleague at lunchtime. Some people like to count their steps with a phone app, but you do not need any special equipment – just comfortable shoes.

The most important thing is to start slowly and keep going. A short walk every day is better than one very long walk once a month. After a few weeks, many people find that they look forward to their daily walk.

questions.q: Health organisations usually advise adults to do at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "advise adults to do at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise every week" → TRUE.

questions.q: During a brisk walk, you should be too out of breath to talk.
questions.explain: Bài viết giải thích "brisk" là đi đủ nhanh để thở mạnh hơn một chút "but you can still talk" – vẫn nói chuyện được → FALSE.

questions.q: Walking in the morning is better than walking in the evening.
questions.explain: Bài viết chỉ nói đi bộ ngoài trời lúc có ánh sáng ban ngày có thể giúp ngủ ngon, không so sánh buổi sáng với buổi tối → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT given as a way to walk more?
options: Getting off the bus one stop early
Taking the stairs instead of the lift
Walking with a colleague at lunchtime
questions.explain: Bài viết gợi ý xuống xe buýt sớm một trạm, đi cầu thang bộ, đi bộ cùng đồng nghiệp giờ trưa; không nhắc đến việc dắt chó đi dạo.

questions.q: What is the writer's main advice in the last paragraph?
options: Walk a very long way once a month.
Buy special equipment before you start.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "start slowly and keep going. A short walk every day is better than one very long walk once a month".

readings.title: Street Food Around the World
readings.summaryVi: Đồ ăn đường phố có mặt ở khắp nơi trên thế giới: rẻ, nhanh, mang đậm văn hóa địa phương; bài viết cũng nhắc đến vấn đề vệ sinh và cách chọn quầy ăn an toàn.
readings.summaryEn: Street food can be found all over the world: it is cheap, fast and full of local culture; the article also mentions hygiene and how to choose a safe stall.
readings.text:
In cities all over the world, you can buy food on the street. In Mexico, people eat tacos from small stands. In Turkey, you can buy hot bread rings covered in sesame seeds. And in Vietnam, many people start the day with a bowl of noodle soup at a small stall on the pavement.

Why is street food so popular? First, it is usually cheap, so students and workers can eat well without spending much money. Second, it is fast. You can buy something on your way to work and eat it in a few minutes. Third, many people say that street food is the best way to learn about a country's culture, because the recipes are often very old and are passed down in families.

For many sellers, a food stall is also an important business. With a small cart and a few pots, a person can earn money for the whole family. In some cities, street food is so famous that it attracts tourists from other countries.

However, some visitors worry about food safety. Here are a few simple tips. Choose a stall where many local people are eating, because busy stalls usually sell fresh food. Watch how the food is cooked, and choose dishes that are served very hot. If you have a weak stomach, be careful with ice and raw vegetables.

With a little care, street food can be one of the most enjoyable parts of any trip.

questions.q: Street food is usually expensive.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "it is usually cheap" – đồ ăn đường phố thường rẻ → FALSE.

questions.q: Many street food recipes are passed down in families.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the recipes are often very old and are passed down in families" → TRUE.

questions.q: Street food sellers must have a licence in most cities.
questions.explain: Bài viết không nói gì về giấy phép bán hàng → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why does the writer suggest choosing a busy stall?
options: Busy stalls usually sell fresh food.
questions.explain: Bài viết: chọn quầy có nhiều người địa phương ăn "because busy stalls usually sell fresh food".

questions.q: What should people with a weak stomach be careful with?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "If you have a weak stomach, be careful with ice and raw vegetables". Món nóng thì lại được khuyên nên chọn.

readings.title: Why Teenagers Find It Hard to Wake Up
readings.summaryVi: Đồng hồ sinh học của thanh thiếu niên lùi muộn hơn nên khó ngủ sớm và khó dậy sớm; bài viết giải thích nguyên nhân và các cách giúp ngủ đủ giấc.
readings.summaryEn: Teenagers' body clocks shift later, so they find it hard to fall asleep early and to get up early; the article explains why and suggests ways to get enough sleep.
readings.text:
Many parents complain that their teenage children stay up late and then cannot get out of bed in the morning. It is easy to think that teenagers are simply lazy. However, sleep scientists say that the real reason is biological.

Everyone has a body clock that tells us when to feel sleepy and when to feel awake. During the teenage years, this clock moves later. As a result, many teenagers do not feel tired until eleven o'clock at night or even later. At the same time, most still need around eight to ten hours of sleep a night. If school starts early, they simply do not get enough rest.

Lack of sleep can have serious effects. Tired students find it harder to concentrate and remember new information. They may also feel more stressed or get angry more easily. Some research suggests that sleepy teenagers are more likely to have accidents when they ride a bike or drive.

For this reason, some schools have experimented with starting lessons later in the morning. Teachers in these schools often report that students are more alert in class.

Teenagers can also help themselves. Experts recommend going to bed at the same time every night, even at weekends, and avoiding bright screens for an hour before sleep. Getting some daylight in the morning can also help the body clock to stay on time.

questions.q: Sleep scientists believe that teenagers who sleep late are usually lazy.
questions.explain: Bài viết: dễ nghĩ rằng thanh thiếu niên lười, "However, sleep scientists say that the real reason is biological" – lý do là sinh học, không phải lười → FALSE.

questions.q: Most teenagers need around eight to ten hours of sleep a night.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "most still need around eight to ten hours of sleep a night" → TRUE.

questions.q: All schools in the country now start lessons later in the morning.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói "some schools have experimented with starting lessons later"; không có thông tin tất cả các trường đã đổi giờ → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: According to the text, what happens to the body clock during the teenage years?
options: It becomes the same as an adult's.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "During the teenage years, this clock moves later" – đồng hồ sinh học lùi muộn hơn, nên các phương án còn lại sai.

questions.q: Which piece of advice is given to teenagers?
options: Use a phone in bed to relax.
Go to bed at the same time every night.
questions.explain: Chuyên gia khuyên "going to bed at the same time every night, even at weekends". Bài khuyên tránh màn hình sáng và NÊN đón ánh sáng buổi sáng, nên B và D sai; A trái với lời khuyên giữ giờ cố định.

readings.title: The Magic of Night Markets
readings.summaryVi: Chợ đêm là nơi mua sắm, ăn uống và gặp gỡ ở nhiều nước châu Á; bài viết nói về sức hút, lợi ích kinh tế và những thách thức như rác thải, tiếng ồn.
readings.summaryEn: Night markets are places to shop, eat and meet people in many Asian countries; the article describes their appeal, their economic benefits and challenges such as litter and noise.
readings.text:
When the sun goes down in many Asian cities, quiet streets and car parks suddenly come to life. Stalls appear, lights are switched on, and the smell of grilled food fills the air. Welcome to the night market.

Night markets have a long history in countries such as Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. In hot climates, it makes sense to shop and eat in the evening, when the temperature is lower. For many families, a trip to the night market is a weekly tradition.

The main attraction for most visitors is the food. Visitors can try dozens of local dishes in one evening, often for very low prices. But night markets also sell clothes, phone cases, toys and handmade souvenirs, and many people enjoy bargaining with the sellers.

Night markets are important for the local economy, too. Renting a stall is much cheaper than opening a shop, so they give young people and small businesses a chance to start their own business. Some successful sellers later open restaurants.

However, night markets also create problems. Residents who live nearby sometimes complain about noise and traffic late at night. Large amounts of plastic bags and food boxes are thrown away every evening. In response, some markets now ask sellers to use paper packaging and have added more bins and recycling points.

Despite these challenges, night markets remain one of the best ways to experience the everyday life of a city.

questions.q: In hot countries, the evening is a comfortable time to shop.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "In hot climates, it makes sense to shop and eat in the evening, when the temperature is lower" → TRUE.

questions.q: Food at night markets is usually expensive.
questions.explain: Bài viết nói khách có thể thử nhiều món "often for very low prices" – giá thường rất rẻ → FALSE.

questions.q: Most night markets open every day of the year.
questions.explain: Bài viết không nói chợ đêm mở bao nhiêu ngày trong năm; chỉ nói với nhiều gia đình, đi chợ đêm là thói quen hằng tuần → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why are night markets good for young people who want to start a business?
options: They do not have to pay any taxes.
Renting a stall costs much less than opening a shop.
The government gives them free training.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Renting a stall is much cheaper than opening a shop" nên chợ đêm cho người trẻ cơ hội khởi nghiệp. Các phương án khác không được nhắc tới.

questions.q: How have some markets responded to the problem of waste?
options: By asking sellers to use paper packaging
By charging visitors an entry fee
questions.explain: Bài viết: "some markets now ask sellers to use paper packaging and have added more bins and recycling points".

readings.title: Can an App Teach You a Language?
readings.summaryVi: Ứng dụng học ngoại ngữ giúp luyện tập đều đặn và tiện lợi, nhưng khó thay thế hoàn toàn việc nói chuyện thật; bài viết gợi ý cách kết hợp hiệu quả.
readings.summaryEn: Language-learning apps make regular practice easy and convenient, but they cannot fully replace real conversation; the article suggests how to combine the two effectively.
readings.text:
Millions of people now use apps on their phones to learn a new language. They complete short lessons on the bus, during their lunch break or just before bed. But can an app really teach you to speak a language?

Apps have some clear advantages. They are usually cheap or free, and you can study whenever you have a few minutes. Many apps send reminders and give points or rewards, which encourages users to practise every day. Regular practice is important, because the brain remembers new words better when it sees them several times over a period of days.

Apps are especially good for building vocabulary and learning basic grammar. Some also use speech recognition to check your pronunciation.

However, there are limits to what an app can do. Real conversations are fast and unpredictable. People speak with different accents, use slang and interrupt each other. An app cannot fully prepare you for this. In addition, some learners collect points every day without making much real progress, because the lessons are too easy for them.

Most teachers believe that the best approach is to combine an app with other activities. You could use the app for ten minutes a day to learn new words, then use them in real situations: chatting with a language partner, watching videos without subtitles or writing short messages. In this way, the app becomes a useful tool rather than the whole course.

questions.q: Language apps are usually cheap or free.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "They are usually cheap or free" → TRUE.

questions.q: Apps fully prepare learners for real conversations.
questions.explain: Bài viết: hội thoại thật nhanh và khó đoán, "An app cannot fully prepare you for this" → FALSE.

questions.q: Most language app users stop using the app after one month.
questions.explain: Bài viết không đưa thông tin về việc người dùng bỏ ứng dụng sau bao lâu → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why does the writer say regular practice is important?
options: Apps give more points for daily practice.
The brain remembers words better after seeing them several times over some days.
Teachers check the app every day.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the brain remembers new words better when it sees them several times over a period of days". Điểm thưởng chỉ là cách ứng dụng khuyến khích, không phải lý do việc luyện đều quan trọng.

questions.q: What do most teachers recommend?
options: Using an app instead of a teacher
Studying only with an app for several hours a day
Combining an app with real communication
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the best approach is to combine an app with other activities", ví dụ nói chuyện với bạn học, xem video không phụ đề.

readings.title: My First Part-Time Job
readings.summaryVi: Một sinh viên kể về công việc làm thêm đầu tiên ở quán cà phê: những khó khăn ban đầu, kỹ năng học được và lời khuyên cho người mới đi làm.
readings.summaryEn: A student describes their first part-time job in a café: the early difficulties, the skills they learned and advice for people starting work.
readings.text:
When I was eighteen, I got my first part-time job in a small café near my university. I worked there three evenings a week and on Saturday mornings.

The first week was very difficult. I had to remember the names of more than twenty drinks, and the coffee machine looked very complicated. On my second day, I gave a customer tea instead of hot chocolate. I felt terrible, but the manager just smiled and said, "Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning."

After a month, the job became much easier. I learned how to make drinks quickly, how to use the cash register and how to talk politely to customers, even when they were in a hurry. I also learned to plan my time better, because I had to finish my homework before my evening shifts.

The money was not very good, but it was enough to pay for my books and my bus pass. The best part of the job was my colleagues. We often had dinner together after work, and some of them are still my good friends today.

My advice for anyone starting their first job is simple: ask questions when you don't understand something, and don't worry too much about small mistakes.

questions.q: The writer worked at the café every evening.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "I worked there three evenings a week and on Saturday mornings" – chỉ ba buổi tối mỗi tuần, không phải tối nào cũng làm → FALSE.

questions.q: The manager was angry about the mistake with the drinks.
questions.explain: Người quản lý "just smiled and said, Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning" – không hề tức giận → FALSE.

questions.q: The café was the most popular one near the university.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói đây là "a small café near my university"; không có thông tin quán có đông khách nhất hay không → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What did the writer use the money for?
questions.explain: Bài viết: tiền lương "was enough to pay for my books and my bus pass". Tiền thuê nhà, điện thoại hay kỳ nghỉ không được nhắc tới.

questions.q: What does the writer say was the best part of the job?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "The best part of the job was my colleagues". Tác giả còn nói lương "not very good", nên phương án tiền lương sai.

readings.title: Recycling Starts at Home
readings.summaryVi: Hướng dẫn phân loại rác tại nhà: giấy, nhựa, kim loại, thủy tinh và rác hữu cơ; vì sao cần rửa sạch vật dụng và những thứ không nên bỏ vào thùng tái chế.
readings.summaryEn: A guide to sorting rubbish at home: paper, plastic, metal, glass and food waste; why items should be rinsed and what should not go in the recycling bin.
readings.text:
Many cities now ask people to separate their rubbish at home. This helps more materials to be recycled instead of going to landfill. But what should go in each bin?

Paper and cardboard are usually easy to recycle. Newspapers, cereal boxes and old letters can all go in the paper bin. However, paper that is dirty with food, such as a pizza box with oil on it, should go in the normal rubbish.

Many plastic bottles and food containers can be recycled too, but they need to be empty and clean. A quick rinse with water is usually enough. Metal cans and glass jars are also accepted in most places. Remember to take off the lids first, because they are often made of a different material.

Food waste, such as fruit peel and vegetable leftovers, can be collected separately in some cities. It is turned into compost, which farmers and gardeners use to help plants grow.

Some things should never go in a recycling bin. Batteries, light bulbs and old phones can be dangerous and need special collection points. Many supermarkets have boxes for batteries near the entrance.

It can take a few weeks to get used to sorting your rubbish, but after that it becomes a normal habit.

questions.q: A pizza box with oil on it should go in the paper bin.
questions.explain: Bài viết: giấy bẩn dính thức ăn "such as a pizza box with oil on it, should go in the normal rubbish" – phải bỏ vào rác thường → FALSE.

questions.q: Plastic bottles should be cleaned before they are recycled.
questions.explain: Bài viết: chai nhựa "need to be empty and clean. A quick rinse with water is usually enough" → TRUE.

questions.q: All cities collect food waste separately.
questions.explain: Bài viết: rác thực phẩm được thu gom riêng "in some cities" – chỉ ở một số thành phố, không phải tất cả → FALSE.

questions.q: Why should you take the lids off jars?
options: They are often made of a different material.
They can be used again at home.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "take off the lids first, because they are often made of a different material". Các lý do khác không được nhắc tới.

questions.q: Where can you often take old batteries?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Many supermarkets have boxes for batteries near the entrance". Pin không bao giờ được bỏ vào thùng tái chế hay rác thường vì có thể nguy hiểm.

readings.title: Learning to Swim as an Adult
readings.summaryVi: Nhiều người lớn chưa biết bơi vì ngại hoặc sợ nước; bài viết chia sẻ lợi ích của việc học bơi và cách bắt đầu từ từ để tự tin hơn.
readings.summaryEn: Many adults cannot swim because they feel embarrassed or are afraid of water; the article shares the benefits of learning to swim and how to start slowly and build confidence.
readings.text:
Not everyone learns to swim as a child. Some people grew up far from the sea or a swimming pool, and others had a bad experience in the water when they were young. As adults, many of them feel embarrassed to start.

However, it is never too late to learn. Swimming is a useful life skill, and it is also excellent exercise. It works almost every muscle in the body, but it is gentle on the knees and back, so it is suitable for people of all ages.

Many swimming pools offer special classes for adult beginners. These classes are usually small, and the teachers understand that some students are nervous. In the first lessons, students often stay in the shallow end of the pool. They practise breathing out under the water and floating on their backs before they try to swim any distance.

Progress can be slow at first, and that is normal. Instructors say the most important thing is to come regularly, for example once or twice a week. Many adult learners say that they feel proud and more confident after a few months, not only in the water but also in other parts of their lives.

If you would like to learn, start by asking at your local pool. You might be surprised how many other adults are learning too.

questions.q: Some adults cannot swim because they had a bad experience in the water as children.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "others had a bad experience in the water when they were young" → TRUE.

questions.q: Swimming is bad for people with knee problems.
questions.explain: Bài viết: bơi "is gentle on the knees and back, so it is suitable for people of all ages" – nhẹ nhàng với đầu gối → FALSE.

questions.q: Adult swimming classes are cheaper than children's classes.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh học phí giữa lớp người lớn và lớp trẻ em → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What do students usually do in their first lessons?
options: Practise breathing and floating in the shallow end
Dive from the side of the pool
questions.explain: Bài viết: học viên ở "the shallow end of the pool", tập thở ra dưới nước và nổi ngửa "before they try to swim any distance". Bơi xa, nhảy cầu, thi bơi không được nhắc tới.

questions.q: According to instructors, what is the most important thing?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the most important thing is to come regularly, for example once or twice a week". Không cần bơi mỗi ngày hay học nhanh; tiến bộ chậm lúc đầu là bình thường.

readings.title: Why People Volunteer
readings.summaryVi: Vì sao nhiều người dành thời gian làm tình nguyện: giúp cộng đồng, học kỹ năng mới, gặp gỡ bạn bè và cải thiện sức khỏe tinh thần; kèm lời khuyên chọn hoạt động phù hợp.
readings.summaryEn: Why many people give their time as volunteers: to help the community, learn new skills, make friends and improve their mental health – with tips on choosing the right activity.
readings.text:
Every weekend, millions of people around the world give their time for free. They clean beaches, help in hospitals, teach children to read or cook meals for people who are homeless. Why do they do it?

The most common reason is simple: people want to help others and to make their community a better place. Many volunteers say that they feel they are giving something back, especially if they once received help themselves.

Volunteering can also be useful for the volunteers. Young people often gain skills and experience that look good on a job application, such as teamwork, organisation and communication. Some organisations even provide training, for example in first aid.

There are social benefits, too. Volunteering is a good way to meet people with similar interests, which can be especially valuable for someone who has just moved to a new city or retired from work.

Finally, several studies have found that people who volunteer regularly tend to report higher levels of happiness. Researchers think this may be because helping others gives people a sense of purpose, although they point out that happier people may also be more likely to volunteer in the first place.

If you are thinking about volunteering, choose something that matches your interests and the time you really have. It is better to give two hours a month for a year than ten hours a week for only a few weeks.

questions.q: Most volunteers say their main reason is to help other people.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "The most common reason is simple: people want to help others and to make their community a better place" → TRUE.

questions.q: All volunteer organisations provide first aid training.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Some organisations even provide training" – chỉ một số tổ chức, không phải tất cả → FALSE.

questions.q: Researchers are sure that volunteering makes people happier.
questions.explain: Bài viết nói các nhà nghiên cứu "think this may be because…" và lưu ý người vốn đã hạnh phúc có thể dễ đi tình nguyện hơn – họ không chắc chắn về quan hệ nhân quả → FALSE.

questions.q: Why might volunteering be especially valuable for someone who has just retired?
options: It is a way to meet people with similar interests.
It helps them find a new job.
questions.explain: Bài viết: tình nguyện là cách "to meet people with similar interests, which can be especially valuable for someone who has just moved… or retired". Tình nguyện không được trả lương và không bắt buộc.

questions.q: What advice does the writer give at the end?
options: Volunteer as many hours as possible.
Choose an activity that fits your interests and available time.
Volunteer only when you are young.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "choose something that matches your interests and the time you really have", và làm đều đặn ít giờ tốt hơn làm nhiều trong vài tuần – trái với phương án "càng nhiều giờ càng tốt".

readings.title: Why Do We Dream?
readings.summaryVi: Giấc mơ thường xuất hiện trong giai đoạn ngủ REM; các nhà khoa học đưa ra nhiều giả thuyết về chức năng của giấc mơ nhưng chưa có câu trả lời chắc chắn.
readings.summaryEn: Dreams usually happen during REM sleep; scientists have put forward many theories about what dreams are for, but there is no definite answer yet.
readings.text:
Almost everyone dreams, even people who say they never do. The difference is that some people remember their dreams and others forget them within minutes of waking up.

Scientists know that many of our most vivid dreams happen during a stage of sleep called REM sleep. REM stands for "rapid eye movement", because during this stage our eyes move quickly behind our closed eyelids. Our brain is very active during REM sleep, but most of the muscles in our body are relaxed and cannot move. Many researchers believe this stops us from acting out our dreams.

But why do we dream at all? There is still no single answer. One popular idea is that dreams help the brain to process memories and emotions from the day. Another suggests that dreams allow us to practise reacting to difficult situations in a safe way. A third theory says that dreams may simply be a side effect of the brain's activity during sleep, with no special purpose.

What scientists do agree on is that good sleep is important for both the body and the mind. Adults who regularly sleep too little often find it harder to concentrate and control their mood.

So, the next time you have a strange dream, you can enjoy the mystery. Even the experts are still trying to understand it.

questions.q: People who say they never dream probably do dream but forget it.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Almost everyone dreams, even people who say they never do" – khác biệt là có người quên giấc mơ ngay sau khi thức dậy → TRUE.

questions.q: During REM sleep, the brain is not very active.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Our brain is very active during REM sleep" – não hoạt động mạnh, chỉ có cơ bắp là thả lỏng → FALSE.

questions.q: Children dream more often than adults.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh tần suất mơ giữa trẻ em và người lớn → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What do many researchers believe is the purpose of relaxed muscles during REM sleep?
options: To help us breathe more slowly
To stop us from acting out our dreams
To make our eyes move quickly
questions.explain: Bài viết: cơ bắp thả lỏng, không cử động được, và "this stops us from acting out our dreams". Các phương án khác không được nhắc tới hoặc nhầm với chuyển động của mắt.

questions.q: What does the text say about the reason why we dream?
options: Scientists have proved that dreams process memories.
There are several theories but no single answer.
Dreams have no purpose at all.
Dreams only happen when we are stressed.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "There is still no single answer" rồi nêu ba giả thuyết. Ý "xử lý ký ức" và "không có mục đích" chỉ là các giả thuyết, chưa được chứng minh.

readings.title: A Morning at the Farmers' Market
readings.summaryVi: Một buổi sáng thứ Bảy ở chợ nông sản: người bán là nông dân địa phương, rau quả theo mùa, có thể nếm thử và nói chuyện với người trồng.
readings.summaryEn: A Saturday morning at a farmers' market: the sellers are local farmers, the fruit and vegetables are seasonal, and you can taste them and talk to the growers.
readings.text:
Every Saturday morning, Elena walks to the farmers' market in the center of her town. The market opens at eight o'clock and closes at one, but she likes to go early because the best fruit sells out quickly.

At a farmers' market, the sellers are usually the people who grew the food. Elena buys tomatoes and lettuce from an old farmer called Mr. Diaz, who has a farm about thirty minutes away. He always tells her which vegetables are best that week.

The food changes with the seasons. In summer, there are strawberries, peaches and corn. In autumn, there are apples and pumpkins. Some sellers also bring fresh bread, honey and cheese.

Elena likes the market because she can taste things before she buys them, and she knows that the food is fresh. It is sometimes a little more expensive than the supermarket, but she thinks it is worth it. She also enjoys meeting her neighbors there and listening to the music of a local band.

questions.q: The market is open all day on Saturday.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "The market opens at eight o'clock and closes at one" – chợ chỉ mở buổi sáng đến 1 giờ chiều → FALSE.

questions.q: Mr. Diaz grows the vegetables that he sells.
questions.explain: Bài viết: người bán "are usually the people who grew the food", và Mr. Diaz có trang trại cách khoảng 30 phút → TRUE.

questions.q: Elena always pays with cash at the market.
questions.explain: Bài viết không nhắc đến cách Elena trả tiền → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why does Elena go to the market early?
options: Because the market is less crowded
Because the best fruit sells out quickly
Because the band plays in the morning
Because she works in the afternoon
questions.explain: Bài viết: "she likes to go early because the best fruit sells out quickly" – trái cây ngon nhất bán hết nhanh.

questions.q: What does Elena think about the prices at the market?
options: They are much cheaper than the supermarket.
They are too high to be worth it.
They are sometimes higher, but the food is worth it.
They are the same as the supermarket.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "It is sometimes a little more expensive than the supermarket, but she thinks it is worth it" – đôi khi đắt hơn nhưng xứng đáng.

readings.title: Opening a Bank Account
readings.summaryVi: Kenji mở tài khoản ngân hàng lần đầu ở Mỹ: chuẩn bị giấy tờ, chọn tài khoản thanh toán và tiết kiệm, nhận thẻ ghi nợ.
readings.summaryEn: Kenji opens a bank account in the US for the first time: preparing documents, choosing a checking and a savings account, and getting a debit card.
readings.text:
When Kenji moved to the United States for his new job, one of the first things he needed was a bank account. His company wanted to pay his salary directly into an account every two weeks.

Kenji made an appointment at a bank near his apartment. Before he went, he checked the bank's website to see what documents he needed. He took his passport, a letter from his employer and his lease, which showed his new address.

At the bank, a friendly employee called Mrs. Lopez explained the different accounts. A checking account is for everyday spending and paying bills. A savings account is for money that you want to keep for the future. Kenji decided to open both.

Mrs. Lopez told him that his debit card would arrive by mail in about a week. Until then, he could use the bank's app on his phone to check his balance. Kenji was happy that everything took less than an hour.

questions.q: Kenji's company pays his salary every month.
questions.explain: Bài viết: công ty trả lương "every two weeks" – hai tuần một lần, không phải hằng tháng → FALSE.

questions.q: Kenji used his lease to prove his address.
questions.explain: Bài viết: anh mang "his lease, which showed his new address" → TRUE.

questions.q: Mrs. Lopez has worked at the bank for many years.
questions.explain: Bài viết chỉ nói bà là nhân viên thân thiện, không nói bà làm ở ngân hàng bao lâu → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What is a checking account used for?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "A checking account is for everyday spending and paying bills."

questions.q: How could Kenji check his balance before his card arrived?
options: By visiting the bank every day
By using the bank's app on his phone
By reading letters from the bank
questions.explain: Bài viết: "he could use the bank's app on his phone to check his balance".

readings.title: Taking the Bus in a New City
readings.summaryVi: Hướng dẫn đơn giản để đi xe buýt ở thành phố mới: xem lộ trình trên ứng dụng, mua vé/thẻ, bấm chuông xuống xe, nhường chỗ.
readings.summaryEn: A simple guide to taking the bus in a new city: checking the route in an app, buying a ticket or card, pressing the bell to get off and giving up your seat.
readings.text:
Taking the bus in a new city can feel difficult at first, but it is usually cheap and easy once you know how it works.

First, find out which bus you need. Most cities have a free app or website that shows bus routes and times. You type where you are and where you want to go, and the app tells you which bus to take and where to wait.

Next, think about your ticket. In some cities, you pay the driver with exact change when you get on. In many others, you can buy a travel card and tap it on a machine near the door. A travel card is often cheaper if you take the bus every day.

On the bus, watch the screen or listen for the name of your stop. When your stop is next, press the button or pull the cord to tell the driver. If the bus is busy, offer your seat to older passengers or people with small children. It is a small thing, but it makes the trip nicer for everyone.

questions.q: Bus apps can show you where to wait for your bus.
questions.explain: Bài viết: ứng dụng "tells you which bus to take and where to wait" → TRUE.

questions.q: In every city, you must pay the driver in cash.
questions.explain: Bài viết: chỉ "In some cities" trả tiền mặt cho tài xế; nhiều nơi khác dùng thẻ đi lại → FALSE.

questions.q: Travel cards can also be used on trains.
questions.explain: Bài viết không nói thẻ đi lại có dùng cho tàu hỏa hay không → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why might a travel card be a good choice?
options: It is cheaper if you take the bus every day.
It lets you sit at the front of the bus.
You do not need to tap it.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "A travel card is often cheaper if you take the bus every day."

questions.q: What should you do when your stop is next?
options: Press the button or pull the cord
Wait until the bus stops and then shout
questions.explain: Bài viết: "When your stop is next, press the button or pull the cord to tell the driver."

readings.title: Meeting the Neighbors
readings.summaryVi: Gia đình Amira chuyển đến khu phố mới và làm quen hàng xóm: mang bánh tặng, tiệc nướng cuối tuần, giúp đỡ lẫn nhau.
readings.summaryEn: Amira's family moves to a new neighbourhood and gets to know the neighbours: bringing a cake as a gift, a weekend barbecue and helping each other out.
readings.text:
Last spring, Amira and her family moved into a new house on Maple Street. For the first few weeks, they did not know anyone, and the children felt a little lonely.

One afternoon, their neighbor Mrs. Carter knocked on the door with a plate of cookies. She welcomed them to the street and told them about the park nearby and the best place to buy pizza. Amira was very surprised and happy.

A few days later, Amira baked a cake and took it to the family on the other side of her house. They had two children of the same age as hers, and soon the children were playing together after school.

In July, the neighbors held a barbecue in the street. Everyone brought some food, and Amira's family made rice and chicken. Now, when Amira goes on vacation, Mrs. Carter waters her plants, and when Mrs. Carter is sick, Amira does her shopping. Amira says that good neighbors make a house feel like home.

questions.q: Amira's children felt lonely at first.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the children felt a little lonely" trong những tuần đầu → TRUE.

questions.q: Mrs. Carter brought a cake to Amira's family.
questions.explain: Bài viết: bà Carter mang "a plate of cookies" (bánh quy); chính Amira mới là người nướng bánh kem → FALSE.

questions.q: The street barbecue happens every year.
questions.explain: Bài viết chỉ nói hàng xóm tổ chức tiệc nướng vào tháng Bảy, không nói có diễn ra hằng năm → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What did Mrs. Carter tell the family about?
options: The park and a good place to buy pizza
questions.explain: Bài viết: bà "told them about the park nearby and the best place to buy pizza".

questions.q: How do Amira and Mrs. Carter help each other now?
options: They drive each other to work.
They cook dinner together every week.
They water plants and do shopping for each other.
They look after each other's children.
questions.explain: Bài viết: bà Carter tưới cây khi Amira đi nghỉ, còn Amira đi chợ giúp khi bà Carter ốm.

readings.title: Tipping in the United States
readings.summaryVi: Văn hóa tiền boa ở Mỹ: vì sao nhân viên phục vụ phụ thuộc vào tiền boa, mức thường gặp, khi nào cần và không cần boa, tranh luận hiện nay.
readings.summaryEn: Tipping culture in the US: why restaurant staff depend on tips, the usual amounts, when you should and should not tip, and the current debate.
readings.text:
For many visitors, tipping is one of the most confusing parts of life in the United States. In many countries, a service charge is included in the bill or tipping is optional. In the US, however, a tip is often expected, especially in restaurants.

One reason is that many restaurant servers earn a low basic wage, and tips make up a large part of their income. For table service in a restaurant, customers commonly leave between fifteen and twenty percent of the bill before tax. People also usually tip taxi drivers, hairdressers and hotel staff who carry luggage.

Other situations are less clear. When you buy a coffee at a counter, the payment screen may suggest a tip of fifteen, twenty or twenty-five percent. Many customers feel uncomfortable about this, because they are not receiving table service. Tipping in these situations is generally optional, and choosing "no tip" is not considered rude.

In recent years, some Americans have complained about "tipping fatigue" as more businesses ask for tips. A few restaurants have responded by raising their prices and paying staff a higher wage instead. Whether this approach will spread is still uncertain, but for now, visitors should be ready to add a tip when they eat out.

questions.q: In US restaurants, tips are often an important part of servers' income.
questions.explain: Bài viết: nhiều nhân viên phục vụ có lương cơ bản thấp và "tips make up a large part of their income" → TRUE.

questions.q: It is rude not to tip when you buy coffee at a counter.
questions.explain: Bài viết: boa ở quầy thường là tùy chọn và chọn "no tip" "is not considered rude" → FALSE.

questions.q: Most American restaurants have stopped asking for tips.
questions.explain: Bài viết chỉ nói "A few restaurants" tăng giá thay cho tiền boa, và du khách vẫn nên sẵn sàng boa khi ăn ngoài → FALSE.

questions.q: How much do customers commonly tip for table service?
options: Five to ten percent of the bill
Fifteen to twenty percent of the bill before tax
A fixed amount of five dollars
questions.explain: Bài viết: khách thường để lại "between fifteen and twenty percent of the bill before tax".

questions.q: What does "tipping fatigue" refer to?
options: Servers feeling tired after long shifts
Customers feeling annoyed that more businesses ask for tips
questions.explain: "tipping fatigue" xuất hiện khi người Mỹ phàn nàn "as more businesses ask for tips" – mệt mỏi vì bị xin tiền boa ở quá nhiều nơi.

readings.title: Getting Ready for a Job Interview
readings.summaryVi: Cách chuẩn bị phỏng vấn xin việc: tìm hiểu công ty, chuẩn bị ví dụ theo cách STAR, chuẩn bị câu hỏi cho nhà tuyển dụng, gửi thư cảm ơn.
readings.summaryEn: How to prepare for a job interview: research the company, prepare examples using the STAR method, prepare questions for the employer and send a thank-you note.
readings.text:
A job interview can be stressful, but good preparation makes a big difference. The first step is to learn about the company. Read its website, look at recent news and try to understand what the company does and what it values. Interviewers are often impressed when candidates can connect their own experience to the company's goals.

Next, think about the questions you are likely to hear, such as "Tell me about yourself" or "Describe a problem you solved at work." Many career advisers recommend the STAR method for answering questions about experience: describe the Situation, the Task, the Action you took and the Result. Practising a few examples out loud, with a friend or in front of a mirror, can help you speak more confidently.

It is also important to prepare some questions of your own. Asking about the team, the training or the first few months in the job shows that you are seriously interested. However, it is usually better not to ask about salary in a first interview unless the interviewer mentions it.

Finally, the interview does not end when you leave the room. Sending a short thank-you email the same day is a polite way to remind the interviewer of your interest.

questions.q: The STAR method is used for answering questions about past experience.
questions.explain: Bài viết: chuyên gia khuyên dùng STAR "for answering questions about experience" → TRUE.

questions.q: Candidates should always ask about salary in the first interview.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "it is usually better not to ask about salary in a first interview unless the interviewer mentions it" → FALSE.

questions.q: Most interviews last about one hour.
questions.explain: Bài viết không nhắc đến độ dài buổi phỏng vấn → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why should candidates prepare their own questions?
options: To show that they are seriously interested
To find out about the interviewer's salary
questions.explain: Bài viết: hỏi về nhóm, đào tạo, những tháng đầu "shows that you are seriously interested".

questions.q: What does the writer suggest doing after the interview?
options: Sending a short thank-you email the same day
Posting about it on social media
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Sending a short thank-you email the same day is a polite way to remind the interviewer of your interest."

readings.title: Why It Pays to Learn to Cook
readings.summaryVi: Lợi ích của việc tự nấu ăn: tiết kiệm tiền, kiểm soát nguyên liệu, kỹ năng sống, gắn kết; cách bắt đầu từ vài món đơn giản.
readings.summaryEn: The benefits of cooking for yourself: saving money, controlling the ingredients, life skills and bringing people together; how to start with a few simple dishes.
readings.text:
Many young adults leave home without knowing how to cook more than a few simple dishes. With food delivery apps on every phone, it can seem unnecessary to learn. Yet cooking is one of the most useful skills a person can have.

The most obvious benefit is money. A meal cooked at home usually costs much less than the same meal from a restaurant or delivery service, especially when you add delivery fees and tips. Cooking also lets you control what goes into your food. You can decide how much salt, sugar and oil to use, which makes it easier to eat a balanced diet.

Cooking has social benefits too. Preparing a meal for friends or family is a way of showing care, and eating together gives people time to talk without screens.

The good news is that you do not need to be an expert to start. Begin with three or four dishes that you enjoy, such as a pasta sauce, a stir-fry or a soup, and cook them until you feel confident. Online videos can be helpful, but it is also worth asking older relatives to teach you family recipes. Within a few months, most beginners find that cooking becomes faster, easier and even relaxing.

questions.q: Delivery fees and tips can make food delivery more expensive.
questions.explain: Bài viết: nấu ở nhà rẻ hơn nhiều "especially when you add delivery fees and tips" → TRUE.

questions.q: You need to take a cooking course before you start cooking at home.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "you do not need to be an expert to start" – bắt đầu với 3–4 món quen thuộc → FALSE.

questions.q: Young adults today cook less than their grandparents did.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh thói quen nấu ăn giữa các thế hệ → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: How does cooking help people eat a balanced diet?
options: It lets them control the amount of salt, sugar and oil.
It means they eat more often.
It makes them buy more vegetables.
questions.explain: Bài viết: tự nấu giúp "decide how much salt, sugar and oil to use, which makes it easier to eat a balanced diet".

questions.q: What does the writer recommend for beginners?
options: Learning many difficult dishes at once
Practising a few favorite dishes until they feel confident
questions.explain: Bài viết: bắt đầu với "three or four dishes that you enjoy" và nấu "until you feel confident".

readings.title: When the Coffee Shop Becomes the Office
readings.summaryVi: Vì sao nhiều người làm việc ở quán cà phê: tiếng ồn nền vừa phải, cảm giác có người xung quanh; nhưng cũng có bất tiện và phép lịch sự cần giữ.
readings.summaryEn: Why many people work in cafés: a moderate level of background noise and the feeling of having people around – but there are also drawbacks and some etiquette to follow.
readings.text:
Walk into almost any coffee shop on a weekday morning and you will see people working on laptops. Since more people began working from home, cafés have become popular "third places" – spaces that are neither home nor the office.

Why do people choose to work there? Some say that the gentle background noise of a café helps them concentrate better than the silence of an empty apartment. Others simply like being around people. Working alone at home all day can feel lonely, and seeing others busy at their tables can be motivating.

However, cafés are not perfect offices. Wi-Fi can be slow, power sockets are often limited, and it is difficult to make private phone calls. There are also unwritten rules. Most café owners are happy for customers to work, but they expect them to buy something every few hours, especially at busy times. Taking up a large table for a whole day after buying one small coffee is generally seen as unfair.

Some cafés have responded by offering special tables for laptop users or by limiting Wi-Fi time during lunch. For many remote workers, the solution is to use cafés for a few hours of focused work and keep video meetings for home.

questions.q: Some people find a little noise helps them concentrate.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the gentle background noise of a café helps them concentrate better than the silence" → TRUE.

questions.q: Café owners usually do not allow customers to work on laptops.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Most café owners are happy for customers to work" – chỉ mong khách mua thêm đồ → FALSE.

questions.q: Coffee shops make more money from remote workers than from other customers.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh doanh thu từ người làm việc từ xa với khách khác → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What is a "third place", according to the text?
options: A café that is open all night
A space that is neither home nor the office
The third table in a café
questions.explain: Bài viết định nghĩa "third places – spaces that are neither home nor the office".

questions.q: What is generally seen as unfair?
options: Using a large table all day after buying one small coffee
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Taking up a large table for a whole day after buying one small coffee is generally seen as unfair."

readings.title: The Hidden Cost of Owning a Car
readings.summaryVi: Chi phí thật của việc sở hữu ô tô vượt xa giá mua: khấu hao, bảo hiểm, bảo dưỡng, đỗ xe, nhiên liệu; so sánh với phương án đi chung và giao thông công cộng.
readings.summaryEn: The real cost of owning a car goes far beyond the purchase price: depreciation, insurance, maintenance, parking and fuel; a comparison with car sharing and public transport.
readings.text:
When people decide whether they can afford a car, they usually focus on the purchase price or the monthly loan payment. Yet the price of the car is only the beginning of what it really costs to own one.

The largest hidden expense is often depreciation – the loss in value as a car gets older. A new car can lose a significant share of its value in its first few years, which matters a great deal when the owner eventually sells it. Insurance is another major cost, and it can be especially high for young drivers or people living in cities where accidents and theft are more common.

Then there are the running costs. Fuel or electricity, regular servicing, new tyres and unexpected repairs all add up. In many city centers, parking can cost as much each month as a basic phone and internet plan combined, and some apartment buildings charge extra for a parking space.

None of this means that owning a car is a bad decision. For people in rural areas or with irregular working hours, a car may be essential. But for city dwellers, it is worth comparing the total annual cost of a car with the alternatives: public transport passes, occasional taxis and car-sharing services that charge by the hour. Many people who do this calculation are surprised by how much they could save.

questions.q: Depreciation means that a car loses value as it gets older.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "depreciation – the loss in value as a car gets older" → TRUE.

questions.q: Insurance costs are the same for all drivers.
questions.explain: Bài viết: bảo hiểm có thể "especially high for young drivers or people living in cities" → không giống nhau → FALSE.

questions.q: Electric cars are cheaper to insure than petrol cars.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh phí bảo hiểm xe điện và xe xăng → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest city dwellers should do?
options: Compare the total yearly cost of a car with other options
questions.explain: Bài viết: "it is worth comparing the total annual cost of a car with the alternatives".

questions.q: For whom might a car be essential, according to the text?
options: People who live in city centers
People in rural areas or with irregular working hours
questions.explain: Bài viết: "For people in rural areas or with irregular working hours, a car may be essential."

readings.title: Why Some Habits Stick
readings.summaryVi: Thói quen hình thành qua lặp lại trong cùng bối cảnh; tín hiệu – hành động – phần thưởng; mẹo xây thói quen tốt: bắt đầu nhỏ, gắn với thói quen có sẵn, thay đổi môi trường.
readings.summaryEn: Habits form through repetition in the same context – cue, action, reward; tips for building good habits: start small, attach them to an existing habit and change your environment.
readings.text:
Why is it so easy to check our phones without thinking, yet so hard to start exercising regularly? Psychologists who study habits explain that a habit is a behavior that has become automatic through repetition in a stable context.

A useful way to think about habits is as a loop with three parts: a cue, a routine and a reward. The cue might be a time, a place or a feeling – for example, finishing lunch at your desk. The routine is the behavior itself, such as scrolling through social media. The reward is the small pleasure that follows, which makes the brain more likely to repeat the loop next time.

This explains why good intentions alone rarely change our behavior. Deciding to "exercise more" does not create a cue, and the benefits of exercise often appear weeks later, so there is little immediate reward.

Researchers suggest several practical strategies. First, start small: a five-minute walk is easier to repeat than an hour at the gym. Second, link the new habit to an existing one, such as doing stretches right after brushing your teeth. Third, change your environment so that the good choice is easier – putting running shoes by the door, for example – and the bad choice is harder. How long it takes for a new behavior to feel automatic varies greatly from person to person, so patience is essential.

questions.q: According to the text, a habit is a behavior that has become automatic.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "a habit is a behavior that has become automatic through repetition in a stable context" → TRUE.

questions.q: Deciding to exercise more is usually enough to create a new habit.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "good intentions alone rarely change our behavior" vì không tạo ra tín hiệu và phần thưởng tức thì → FALSE.

questions.q: Every new habit becomes automatic after exactly 21 days.
questions.explain: Bài viết: thời gian để hành vi thành tự động "varies greatly from person to person" – không có con số cố định → FALSE.

questions.q: In the example of finishing lunch at your desk, what part of the habit loop is this?
questions.explain: Bài viết: tín hiệu (cue) có thể là thời gian, địa điểm hay cảm giác – "for example, finishing lunch at your desk".

questions.q: Which strategy involves linking a new habit to an existing one?
options: Putting running shoes by the door
Doing stretches right after brushing your teeth
questions.explain: Bài viết: "link the new habit to an existing one, such as doing stretches right after brushing your teeth".

readings.title: Understanding Procrastination
readings.summaryVi: Trì hoãn không đơn thuần là lười hay quản lý thời gian kém mà thường liên quan đến cảm xúc khó chịu với nhiệm vụ; cách vượt qua: chia nhỏ, bắt đầu 10 phút, tự thông cảm với bản thân.
readings.summaryEn: Procrastination is not simply laziness or poor time management; it is often linked to unpleasant feelings about a task. Ways to overcome it: break the task down, start with 10 minutes and be kind to yourself.
readings.text:
Almost everyone procrastinates sometimes, delaying a task even though they know they will probably regret it later. It is easy to blame laziness or poor time management, but many psychologists now see procrastination mainly as a problem of managing emotions.

When a task makes us feel anxious, bored or uncertain – writing a difficult report, for example – avoiding it brings immediate relief. Checking messages or tidying the desk feels better in the moment. Unfortunately, the relief is short-lived, and as the deadline approaches, stress increases. Some people then feel guilty, which makes the task even more unpleasant and the cycle continues.

Understanding this pattern suggests a different approach. Instead of simply trying harder to be disciplined, it helps to reduce the negative feelings connected with the task. Breaking a large project into small, concrete steps makes it seem less overwhelming. Committing to work on something for just ten minutes can also help, because starting is often the hardest part, and many people continue once they have begun.

Interestingly, being kind to yourself may also reduce procrastination. People who forgive themselves for delaying a task, rather than criticizing themselves harshly, are often more likely to return to it. Procrastination is a common human habit, not a sign of personal failure, and it can be changed with the right strategies.

questions.q: Many psychologists see procrastination mainly as a problem of managing emotions.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "many psychologists now see procrastination mainly as a problem of managing emotions" → TRUE.

questions.q: Avoiding an unpleasant task brings long-lasting relief.
questions.explain: Bài viết: cảm giác nhẹ nhõm "is short-lived" và căng thẳng tăng khi gần hạn → FALSE.

questions.q: Students procrastinate more than office workers.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh mức độ trì hoãn giữa sinh viên và nhân viên văn phòng → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why can committing to work for just ten minutes help?
options: Because ten minutes is enough to finish most tasks
Because starting is often the hardest part
Because it makes people feel guilty
questions.explain: Bài viết: "starting is often the hardest part, and many people continue once they have begun".

questions.q: What does the writer say about being kind to yourself?
options: It may help people return to the task they delayed.
It is a sign of personal failure.
It only works for small tasks.
questions.explain: Bài viết: người tự tha thứ cho mình "are often more likely to return to it" – dễ quay lại làm tiếp hơn.

readings.title: The Economics of "Free" Shipping
readings.summaryVi: Giao hàng "miễn phí" thực chất có chi phí: được tính vào giá, ngưỡng đơn tối thiểu, gói thành viên; tác động tới hành vi mua sắm, lượng hàng trả lại và môi trường.
readings.summaryEn: "Free" delivery actually has costs: they are built into prices, minimum order thresholds and membership schemes; it affects shopping behaviour, the number of returns and the environment.
readings.text:
Few words are as powerful in online retail as "free shipping". Shoppers are often more willing to pay a slightly higher price for a product with free delivery than a lower price plus a separate shipping fee, even when the total cost is the same. Retailers understand this well, which is why free shipping has become one of the most common features of online shopping.

Of course, delivering a parcel is never actually free. Someone has to pay for warehouses, packaging, fuel and drivers. In practice, retailers recover these costs in several ways. Some build them into the prices of their products. Others set a minimum order value, encouraging customers to add extra items to their basket in order to qualify. Membership programs that offer unlimited free delivery for an annual fee are another strategy; once customers have paid, they tend to shop more often with that retailer to get value from their membership.

Free shipping also changes how people shop. When delivery and returns cost nothing, customers may order several sizes of the same item and send back those that do not fit. Handling returns is expensive for retailers, and many returned products cannot be resold as new.

There are environmental consequences as well. Fast, free delivery encourages frequent small orders, which can mean more half-empty vans on the road and more packaging. In response, some companies now offer customers the option of slower delivery or of grouping orders into a single weekly shipment. Whether shoppers will choose these options when speed is still free remains an open question.

questions.q: Shoppers may prefer a higher price with free delivery to a lower price plus a shipping fee.
questions.explain: Bài viết: người mua thường "more willing to pay a slightly higher price for a product with free delivery than a lower price plus a separate shipping fee" → TRUE.

questions.q: Retailers do not need to pay anything for free deliveries.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "delivering a parcel is never actually free" – phải trả kho, bao bì, nhiên liệu, tài xế → FALSE.

questions.q: Most customers choose slower delivery when it is offered.
questions.explain: Bài viết nói việc khách có chọn giao chậm hay không "remains an open question" – không có thông tin rằng đa số chọn → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: How do minimum order values help retailers?
options: They reduce the number of returns.
They encourage customers to buy extra items.
questions.explain: Bài viết: ngưỡng đơn tối thiểu khuyến khích khách "add extra items to their basket in order to qualify".

questions.q: Why are returns a problem for retailers?
options: Returns are expensive and many items cannot be resold as new.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Handling returns is expensive for retailers, and many returned products cannot be resold as new."

readings.title: Noise: The Invisible Pollutant
readings.summaryVi: Ô nhiễm tiếng ồn ảnh hưởng giấc ngủ, căng thẳng và sức khỏe tim mạch; nguồn chính là giao thông; các giải pháp quy hoạch, vật liệu, quy định và hành vi.
readings.summaryEn: Noise pollution affects sleep, stress levels and heart health; the main source is traffic; solutions include urban planning, materials, regulations and changes in behaviour.
readings.text:
When people think about pollution, they usually imagine dirty air or plastic in the sea. Noise is rarely mentioned, partly because it leaves no visible trace. Yet health authorities, including the World Health Organization, recognize environmental noise as a significant risk to public health, particularly in cities.

The most obvious effect of noise is disturbed sleep. Even when people do not fully wake up, noise from traffic or aircraft at night can interrupt the deeper stages of sleep, leaving them tired the next day. Over time, constant noise is associated with chronic stress, and researchers have linked long-term exposure to higher risks of high blood pressure and heart disease. Children's concentration and learning can also be affected when schools are located near busy roads or airports.

In most cities, the main source of environmental noise is road traffic. This suggests a range of solutions. Lower speed limits reduce tyre and engine noise, and quieter road surfaces can make a noticeable difference. Electric vehicles are much quieter at low speeds, although at higher speeds most of the noise comes from tyres rather than engines. Planners can also place offices or shops, rather than bedrooms, along the busiest streets, and use trees and barriers to absorb sound.

Individual choices matter too, from using headphones on public transport to keeping noisy household tasks to daytime hours. Unlike many environmental problems, noise disappears the moment its source stops – which means that, with the right policies, cities can become quieter remarkably quickly.

questions.q: Noise can disturb sleep even when people do not fully wake up.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Even when people do not fully wake up, noise … can interrupt the deeper stages of sleep" → TRUE.

questions.q: At high speeds, most noise from electric vehicles comes from their engines.
questions.explain: Bài viết: ở tốc độ cao "most of the noise comes from tyres rather than engines" → FALSE.

questions.q: Noise pollution is worse in Europe than in Asia.
questions.explain: Bài viết không so sánh mức ô nhiễm tiếng ồn giữa các châu lục → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What is the main source of environmental noise in most cities?
questions.explain: Bài viết: "In most cities, the main source of environmental noise is road traffic."

questions.q: Why does the writer say cities can become quieter "remarkably quickly"?
options: Because noise disappears as soon as its source stops
Because people get used to noise
questions.explain: Bài viết: "noise disappears the moment its source stops" nên với chính sách đúng, thành phố có thể yên tĩnh hơn rất nhanh.

readings.title: How the Weekend Was Invented
readings.summaryVi: Cuối tuần hai ngày là phát minh khá mới: từ ngày nghỉ tôn giáo, thói quen "Thứ Hai thánh", phong trào công đoàn đến tuần làm việc 5 ngày ở thế kỷ 20.
readings.summaryEn: The two-day weekend is a fairly recent invention: from religious days of rest and the habit of "Saint Monday" to the trade union movement and the five-day working week of the 20th century.
readings.text:
For most office workers today, the two-day weekend seems like a natural part of life. Historically, however, it is a fairly recent invention. For centuries, many societies observed a single weekly day of rest, usually for religious reasons, while the other six days were working days.

The change began during the Industrial Revolution in Britain. Factory work was long and exhausting, and some workers simply failed to appear on Mondays, a habit that became known jokingly as "Saint Monday". Employers disliked these unpredictable absences, and over time a compromise emerged: workers would come in reliably on Monday in exchange for finishing early on Saturday afternoon. The "half-holiday" on Saturday gradually spread during the nineteenth century, helped by campaigns from trade unions.

In the United States, a major step came in the 1920s, when some large employers introduced a five-day working week for factory workers. The industrialist Henry Ford was among the best known, adopting a five-day, forty-hour week in his factories in 1926. Supporters argued that rested workers were more productive, and that people with free time would also spend more money – including on leisure activities and consumer goods. During the following decades, the two-day weekend became standard across much of the industrialized world.

Today, some companies are experimenting with four-day weeks, and the debate echoes earlier arguments about productivity and well-being. History suggests that the length of the working week is not fixed but reflects the economic and social choices of each era.

questions.q: For centuries, many societies had only one weekly day of rest.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "many societies observed a single weekly day of rest" → TRUE.

questions.q: "Saint Monday" was an official holiday created by employers.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Saint Monday" là cách gọi đùa thói quen công nhân tự nghỉ thứ Hai, và chủ lao động "disliked these unpredictable absences" → không phải ngày nghỉ chính thức → FALSE.

questions.q: Henry Ford was the first employer in the world to introduce a five-day week.
questions.explain: Bài viết chỉ nói Ford "was among the best known" trong số các chủ lao động áp dụng tuần 5 ngày, không nói ông là người đầu tiên → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What compromise developed between workers and employers in Britain?
options: Workers would come on Monday in exchange for finishing early on Saturday.
Workers would work on Sundays for extra pay.
Employers would close factories on Mondays.
Workers would take a longer lunch break.
questions.explain: Bài viết: công nhân đi làm đều vào thứ Hai "in exchange for finishing early on Saturday afternoon".

questions.q: Which argument did supporters of the five-day week make?
options: Rested workers would be more productive and spend more money.
Trade unions would become less powerful.
questions.explain: Bài viết: người ủng hộ cho rằng "rested workers were more productive" và người có thời gian rảnh "would also spend more money".

readings.title: Too Many Choices?
readings.summaryVi: Ý tưởng "mệt mỏi vì quyết định" và "quá nhiều lựa chọn": bằng chứng còn tranh cãi; cách đơn giản hóa lựa chọn hằng ngày một cách thực tế.
readings.summaryEn: The ideas of "decision fatigue" and "too much choice": the evidence is still debated; practical ways to simplify everyday choices.
readings.text:
Modern life involves a remarkable number of decisions, from which of dozens of breakfast cereals to buy to which of hundreds of streaming shows to watch. Some writers argue that this abundance comes at a cost. They point to two popular ideas: that making many decisions gradually wears down our ability to choose well – often called "decision fatigue" – and that having too many options can make people less satisfied, or even unable to choose at all.

Both ideas have intuitive appeal. Most of us have felt exhausted after a long day of choices, or stood in front of a supermarket shelf unsure what to pick. However, the scientific evidence is more mixed than popular articles sometimes suggest. Some well-known experiments have proved difficult to repeat, and reviews of the research suggest that the effect of large choice sets depends heavily on the situation – for example, on whether people already know what they like and how easy the options are to compare.

This does not mean the ideas are useless. Even if the effects are smaller and less universal than once claimed, many people find that reducing unnecessary decisions makes daily life feel calmer. Common strategies include planning meals for the week in advance, keeping a simple routine for mornings, and deciding in advance on a few trusted brands. Businesses, too, have learned that presenting options clearly – with sensible defaults and helpful comparisons – can make customers more comfortable with their choices.

The broader lesson may be that choice itself is neither good nor bad. What matters is whether people have the information and structure they need to choose with confidence.

questions.q: According to the text, the scientific evidence for decision fatigue is completely clear.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "the scientific evidence is more mixed than popular articles sometimes suggest" – chưa rõ ràng → FALSE.

questions.q: Some well-known experiments on choice have been difficult to repeat.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "Some well-known experiments have proved difficult to repeat" → TRUE.

questions.q: People who plan their meals in advance are healthier.
questions.explain: Bài viết chỉ nói lên kế hoạch bữa ăn giúp cuộc sống "feel calmer", không nói gì về sức khỏe → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: According to research reviews, what does the effect of large choice sets depend on?
options: The situation, such as whether people know what they like
questions.explain: Bài viết: tác động "depends heavily on the situation – for example, on whether people already know what they like and how easy the options are to compare".

questions.q: What is the writer's main conclusion?
options: More choice always makes people happier.
Choice is neither good nor bad; information and structure matter.
questions.explain: Bài viết kết luận: "choice itself is neither good nor bad. What matters is whether people have the information and structure they need".
